es.title: Las gafas inteligentes y la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual
es.summary: Las gafas inteligentes y la inteligencia artificial están abriendo nuevas posibilidades para las personas con discapacidad visual. Estas herramientas permiten reconocer establecimientos, leer textos y obtener descripciones del entorno mediante indicaciones de audio. El caso de Daniel Álvarez, que perdió la visión a los 15 años, muestra cómo la tecnología puede facilitar algunas tareas cotidianas. […] La entrada Las gafas inteligentes y la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Las gafas inteligentes y la inteligencia artificial están abriendo nuevas posibilidades para las personas con discapacidad visual. Estas herramientas permiten reconocer establecimientos, leer textos y obtener descripciones del entorno mediante indicaciones de audio.

El caso de Daniel Álvarez, que perdió la visión a los 15 años, muestra cómo la tecnología puede facilitar algunas tareas cotidianas. Su experiencia, recogida en un reportaje publicado por El Periódico el 25 de octubre de 2026, pone el foco en la utilidad de estos dispositivos para ganar autonomía.

Daniel Álvarez tiene 30 años, estudia Derecho en la Universitat Oberta de Catalunya (UOC) y trabaja en la ONCE. Tras perder la visión por un desprendimiento de retina irreversible, ha incorporado diferentes herramientas tecnológicas a su vida diaria.

Entre ellas destacan las gafas inteligentes, que incorporan cámaras y altavoces. Gracias a las aplicaciones compatibles, puede obtener información sobre los lugares y objetos que tiene delante.

Por ejemplo, estas gafas pueden ayudarle a distinguir si un establecimiento es un supermercado o una peluquería. También permiten leer textos, identificar colores y conocer detalles de objetos o prendas de ropa.

Sin embargo, sus posibilidades todavía tienen limitaciones. La descripción del entorno no siempre es completamente precisa y depende de la información que capta la cámara y de la interpretación que realiza el sistema.

Daniel utiliza, entre otras herramientas, ScribeMe, una aplicación que describe mediante inteligencia artificial las imágenes captadas por las cámaras de las gafas.

Las aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial no se limitan a describir objetos o espacios. También pueden contribuir a mejorar la accesibilidad de documentos y materiales educativos.

En el caso de Daniel, estas herramientas le permiten adaptar información que no está disponible en un formato accesible. Por ejemplo, puede transformar gráficos de ejercicios académicos en descripciones textuales que pueda comprender mediante su lector de pantalla.

Además, utiliza la inteligencia artificial para crear aplicaciones adaptadas a sus propias necesidades.

Estas posibilidades muestran que la tecnología puede facilitar el acceso a la educación, al trabajo y a la información. No obstante, para aprovecharlas es importante que las aplicaciones y los contenidos digitales sean accesibles desde su diseño.

Aunque las gafas inteligentes ofrecen nuevas posibilidades, no sustituyen a las herramientas tradicionales de orientación y movilidad.

Daniel continúa utilizando su bastón y las técnicas de orientación que conoce. Las gafas le aportan información adicional sobre su entorno, pero no garantizan una descripción completa ni una orientación espacial precisa.

Esta distinción es importante. Reconocer un establecimiento o leer un cartel puede resultar útil durante un desplazamiento, pero no equivale a detectar todos los obstáculos ni a identificar con precisión cada elemento de la vía pública.

Por ello, es fundamental conocer las capacidades y limitaciones de cada dispositivo antes de incorporarlo a las actividades cotidianas.

El Centro de Tiflotecnología e Innovación de la ONCE ha evaluado las gafas inteligentes Ray-Ban Meta y su aplicación Meta AI para analizar su posible utilidad para personas con ceguera o discapacidad visual grave. Su evaluación constituye una referencia especializada para conocer las posibilidades de esta tecnología.

La experiencia de Daniel refleja cómo la combinación de inteligencia artificial, dispositivos inteligentes y herramientas de accesibilidad puede facilitar distintas actividades de la vida diaria.

Sin embargo, la tecnología por sí sola no elimina todas las barreras. Es necesario que las soluciones sean fiables, accesibles y adaptadas a las necesidades reales de las personas con discapacidad visual.

También resulta importante que su desarrollo tenga en cuenta la experiencia de quienes las utilizan. La participación de las propias personas con discapacidad permite identificar necesidades concretas y mejorar la utilidad de estas herramientas.

En definitiva, las gafas inteligentes y la inteligencia artificial representan nuevas oportunidades para acceder a la información y desenvolverse con mayor autonomía. Su utilidad dependerá de que sigan mejorando y se integren como un complemento de los recursos de apoyo ya existentes.

Fuentes: El Periódico: reportaje sobre Daniel Álvarez y las nuevas tecnologías para personas con discapacidad , Centro de Tiflotecnología e Innovación de la ONCE: evaluación de las gafas inteligentes Ray-Ban Meta .

en.title: Apple’s best MacBook Pro decision this week had nothing to do with touch
en.summary: Apple’s new touchscreen MacBook Pro brings plenty of welcome upgrades, but one of the best things about this week’s launch is what the company decided not to change. more…
en.body:
Apple’s new touchscreen MacBook Pro brings plenty of welcome upgrades, but one of the best things about this week’s launch is what the company decided not to change.

Was I aching for a touchscreen Mac? Not particularly. But I can see how useful it might be for a great deal of users, and I’m happy that their day has finally come. Or will come, starting November 6 .

But I’ve been aching for a new Mac. Though my 2023 M2 Pro 16-inch MacBook Pro is still a great machine, its 16GB of RAM is starting to feel a bit cramped. Past me knew this was a mistake.

With the prospect of a revamped MacBook Pro just around the corner, I spent the past few weeks excited about the possibility of biting the bullet and splurging for a new one, even though there had been very conflicting rumors about which chips it would pack .

Although in my heart of hearts I had acquiesced to the idea that the new touchscreen MacBook Pro would get the same chips as the current non-touchscreen line, I was also holding on to the hope that Apple would throw in some performance gains to sweeten the rumored $400 premium deal it would carry.

Right? Right?

Well, no.

Performance-wise, the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is identical to the non-touchscreen models, though there is a case to be made that its redesigned thermal system could make it run faster despite using the same chip, though the changes appear to be aimed more at keeping the display cool than improving heat dissipation. Time, and reviews, will tell.

Which makes Apple’s decision to keep the non-touchscreen M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pro for sale all that more welcome and unexpected.

Even when Apple introduced the Touch Bar back in 2016, the only non-Touch Bar option left was the entry-level 13-inch MacBook Pro. If you wanted a more powerful Mac or a 15-inch model, you had to get with the program and pony up the extra $300 for the 13-inch model with Touch Bar, or $400 for the redesigned 15-inch model.

Yes, there is plenty new with the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. Tandem OLED display, improved thermal performance, thinner, lighter design, slimmer bezels, redesigned audio system, Dynamic Island (debatable for some, I know), and even the return of the glowing Apple logo (woo!) on the lid are all welcome additions. Oh yeah, and “ it has touch as well. ”

Put all of that together, and the $400 premium is arguably not that unreasonable.

But if, like me, these improvements feel secondary to the performance boost you’re prioritizing for this particular upgrade, getting those same specs for effectively $400 less (or using those $400 for better specs!) feels like a pretty great deal for all parties involved, future me included.

Will future me have preferred that I wait for the M7 generation? Possibly. But then again, waiting for the perfect moment to upgrade is what got me into this situation in the first place, recent price hikes and all.

en.title: You don’t need to believe in a god to get a religious exemption from using AI at work
en.summary: David Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator, recently earned a religious exemption from using AI in the workplace.
en.body:
Pope Leo XIV has decried AI as a threat to human dignity , but it’s not just the devoutly faithful who might worry about how AI squares with their beliefs. David Durman, a nontheistic humanist, recently secured a religious exemption from using AI in the workplace.

“Humanism is a collection of beliefs about the human experience and how humans interact with the world,” Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator, told TechCrunch. It centers on “human well-being and flourishing, both individually and collectively … and implores a person to try to improve both their well-being and their flourishing as well as the others around them.”

As he watched AI grow more popular in daily life, Durman sought out the American Humanist Association (AHA) — a nonprofit advancing secular humanism — to investigate how he could gain legal protections against having to use AI at work. He believes that using the technology runs counter to his beliefs.

“The way we become moral actors for ourselves and for others is through the active application of our minds, and the diminishing of that [through AI use] is going to necessarily have a negative impact on our ability to do so,” he said, reflecting on how overreliance on AI might affect critical thinking.

In a statement published by the AHA earlier this week, Durman wrote, “AI is interfering with people’s ability to earn a living, the environmental costs spell disaster for humanity and our planet, and its supplanting and theft of human creativity threaten elements of our culture like art and literature that make society flourish.”

Humanism is not anti-religious, but it tends to appeal to people who are skeptical of a god or other supernatural power yet still seek a scientific and moral framework to ground themselves in.

“Concern about AI and human dignity can run through several different faiths and traditions, whether that’s Catholic teachings, or Universalism, or Humanism, and we want Humanists or nontheists to know that they fall into these categories — that they are also protected by the law at work,” Alexandria Huiskens, staff attorney at the AHA, told TechCrunch.

Durman is the first humanist to secure workplace accommodations that allow him to abstain from AI use, and one of the first people to publicly discuss their pursuit of these protections. He was inspired to seek them when he read that Erin Maus , a Unitarian Universalist and software engineer, was able to secure similar protections for herself.

“For me, this was about me and my convictions,” Durman said. “I’m obviously not trying to tell people how to think or feel … But I do hope that it encourages people who have similar concerns to pursue not necessarily religious exemption, but pursue their concerns to the best of their ability where they feel is the most appropriate.”

University of Kentucky spokesperson Jay Blanton told TechCrunch that the institution reviews requests for religious accommodations on an individual basis, considering the employee’s job responsibilities and the circumstances of the request.

“In this case, the university determined that an accommodation could be provided while allowing the employee to continue performing the essential functions of their position,” Blanton said in a statement. “As technology and job responsibilities evolve, accommodations may be reviewed to ensure they remain reasonable and workable.”

Maus’ situation is especially unusual, since it has become rare for software engineers to write code without any AI assistance. But in Durman’s administrative role, in which he supports researchers applying for grants, he has not been required to use AI at work. Like many workers across fields, some of his colleagues and leadership have recommended that employees try out these tools, so he sought to secure his exemption now, in case the suggestion becomes a mandate in the future.

“I hope that if [others] have similar feelings, that they feel encouraged to pursue some kind of resolution,” Durman said.

en.title: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says — but first, it will spend big
en.summary: Amazon wants to be the king of AI cloud computing and become the first $1 trillion revenue business. But to do that it will have to continue on its capex spending spree, its CEO said Thursday.
en.body:
Andy Jassy has made it known that he believes AWS can be a trillion-dollar revenue business. During Amazon’s quarterly earnings call on Thursday, he repeated this ambition.

“What we’re building at Amazon is unlike anything that’s ever been seen before. There has never been a business with a trillion dollars of annual revenue,” he said.

However, before the cloud business gets there, Amazon is going to have ramp up its capital expenditures to build out the infrastructure necessary to support that blossoming business.

“We still expect 2026 cash capex of approximately $220 billion — the majority for AWS — and expect to spend meaningfully more in 2027, with a clear line of sight to attract its financial returns,” Jassy revealed on Thursday.

Amazon’s big spending on its AI infrastructure buildout has been an ongoing source of concern for investors this year. Indeed, during Thursday’s call, Wall Street analysts repeatedly asked Jassy to explain the spending, the signals that the growth really will come, and the profit margins expected.

Jassy told them it was all money well spent because the e-commerce giant planned to capitalize on a historic moment in global cloud demand driven by AI. AWS revenue increased 39 percent from the year-ago quarter, a trend of steady growth for the sixth straight quarter .

And the CEO forecast on the call that it would increase by 40% not just next year, but in 2028, too.

“AWS is a $184 billion annualized revenue run-rate business, and yet the opportunity remains extraordinary,” the CEO enthused. “With our continued pace of innovation, new core and AI functionality, enterprises wanting to run their core and AI workloads in AWS, and the amount of capacity that we’re adding each year, we believe that AWS can grow north of 40 percent in each 2027 and in 2028, and be a trillion-dollar revenue business in the next five to 10 years.”

Jassy added that the company was “in the very early days” of AI adoption by the enterprise and said that, so far, the “strategy is working.”

Later, when questioned why the investment needed to grow AWS was so substantial, Jassy characterized the AI boom as a “once in a lifetime opportunity” that required, and was worth, such a big financial commitment now.

“We’re going to invest to continue being the leader,” he said. “We can fund this plan, and I think it will forever change the size of Amazon. It will forever change our revenue.”

Investors, however, remained concerned. Shares were down about 6% on Thursday in after-market trading.

The AI boom has been a mixed blessing for the cloud industry, since the AI services that undergird the boom are supported by cloud infrastructure. Like Amazon, other cloud providers are spending big but also earning big. Microsoft, for instance, just posted yet more record-breaking revenue growth, driven largely by its cloud business. It, too, has spent a bundle .

en.title: Report: Apple expected to ship up to 1.5 million OLED touchscreen MacBook Pros in 2027
en.summary: A new report from TrendForce explores Apple’s impact on the OLED notebook market following the launch of its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, and the company’s own shipment prospects for 2027. Here are the details. more…
en.body:
A new report from TrendForce explores Apple’s impact on the OLED notebook market following the launch of its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, and the company’s own shipment prospects for 2027. Here are the details.

Apple yesterday announced the new touchscreen MacBook Pro, which features the same tandem OLED technology it first introduced with the M4 iPad Pro in 2024.

With two OLED layers stacked on top of each other, the technology delivers higher brightness than conventional single-layer OLED displays, while maintaining the deep blacks, high contrast ratios, and power efficiency that OLED is known for.

And while yesterday’s announcement made it official, Apple’s first touchscreen Mac has long been rumored through leaks, reports, and supply chain analyses.

In September 2025, for instance, The Elec reported that Samsung Display was preparing to begin mass production of 14-inch and 16-inch OLED panels for Apple’s MacBook Pro in the second quarter of 2026, with an estimated annual output of 2–3 million units.

Two months later, TrendForce predicted that OLED notebook market share would reach up to 12% between 2027 and 2028, partly driven by Apple’s expected adoption of the technology.

Then, earlier this year, TrendForce published an OLED roadmap predicting that Apple would introduce OLED displays to the MacBook Pro lineup in 2026, followed by the MacBook Air in 2029 ( pushed back from 2027 ).

Now, TrendForce has published a new report with new shipment forecasts for Apple’s OLED MacBook Pro and the broader OLED notebook market.

According to the firm, Apple is expected to ship between 1.2 million and 1.5 million units of the new MacBook Pro in 2027. Meanwhile, global OLED notebook shipments are projected to “grow nearly 40% YoY in 2026, followed by another increase of more than 40% in 2027.”

From the report:

Until now, the OLED notebook market has been driven primarily by Windows-based brands such as Lenovo, HP, and ASUS, which have gradually expanded their OLED offerings across different price segments. Apple’s arrival is expected to give the market additional momentum, encouraging brands to prioritize OLED models in their product roadmaps while strengthening consumer acceptance of the technology. This, in turn, could pave the way for broader OLED adoption in notebook displays.

TrendForce also notes that the “new MacBook Pro’s premium starting price of US$2,899 for the 14-inch model, coupled with its initial availability alongside existing Mini-LED models, could temper near-term replacement demand.”

As for Apple’s first OLED MacBook Air, now expected to debut in 2029, TrendForce says LG Display, BOE, and TCL CSOT are currently competing to become display suppliers for the upcoming model, as the companies continue developing their OLED manufacturing capabilities.

Finally, TrendForce projects that global OLED notebook shipments will reach 46.6 million units by 2030, though year-over-year growth will slow to 30.8%, following a peak of 42.8% in 2028.

To read TrendForce’s full report, follow this link .

en.title: Voice-enabled Makeup Assistant
en.summary: This innovative app offers audio feedback on the user’s foundation, eyeshadow and lipstick application, creating a more accessible beauty experience for the Blind and visually impaired. How It Works: The AI-powered Voice-enabled Makeup Assistant leverages machine learning and voice instruction technologies to learn your preferences and provide audio feedback when you ask. After you apply your foundation, eyeshadow or lipstick, the app will access your phone’s front camera to scan your face. Using artificial intelligence, it identifies the makeup applied to your face, eyes and lips and assesses the uniformity and boundaries of application and coverage. If there are suggested areas to touch up, the virtual assistant identifies them and makes audible recommendations so you can adjust your look. After your touch up, the app scans your face again and provides feedback on the accuracy of application.

en.title: Fan-fiction site Archive of Our Own (AO3) could be offline for up to 4 weeks after security incident
en.summary: The site has such a passionate user base that, within two hours of the announcement, its status page's posts had garnered millions of views (and much panicked commentary) across social media.
en.body:
Posted:

Archive of our Own (AO3), the popular site where fans publish and read stories about their favorite characters and worlds, has bad news for its community. After going offline for what was supposed to be routine overnight maintenance, the site says it could stay online for almost a whole month.

AO3 did not initially share details about what caused the outage, but published a longer statement hours after announcing that the site would likely be down for two to four weeks.

“Earlier today, we detected evidence of a security incident on AO3,” the statement reads . “We are still in the early stages of response to this security incident and determining its scope. AO3 will remain down while we continue investigating and addressing what has been found so far.”

AO3 is a project of the nonprofit Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), which relies on volunteers and donations to keep the site afloat. The site has such a passionate user base that, within two hours of the announcement that it would go offline, its status page’s posts had garnered millions of views (and much panicked commentary) across social media.

“While we currently don’t believe that the user database was stolen, we are also unable to rule it out. The AO3 database contains account information that may include your username, email address, IP address, and a hashed version of your password,” the OTW added.

Though AO3 stores user passwords by using an industry-standard hashing technique, the site recommended that as a precaution, users should change their passwords on any other sites where they may have used the same password.

Some fans may suspect this issue is related to last week’s “ PHP Armageddon ,” when tools from OpenAI and Google Wiz uncovered two critical flaws in PHP, the programming language that runs the behind-the-scenes software of about 70% of the internet . But AO3 is not among that majority. Instead, the site is built on a different framework (a toolkit for running websites), Ruby on Rails, so the outage is unlikely to be related.

OTW and AO3 did not reply to requests for comment.

Updated, 10/29/26, 9:45 PM ET, after OTW published a statement about the nature of the outage.

en.title: Microsoft fixes a Windows 11 annoyance as PC revenue declines
en.summary: The latest update also brings a cloud recovery option for PCs that won't boot.
en.body:
Microsoft is beginning the rollout of a Windows 11 preview update that finally addresses a persistent power user complaint with the operating system: the right-click menu that obliterated years of muscle memory on command locations and hid others behind an additional click. The timing is notable, as the announcement comes alongside Microsoft's quarterly financial report, which showed a continued decline in the business of selling Windows licenses for new PCs.

The preview update, KB5127936 , is cumulative for Windows 11 versions 26H2 and 25H2. The update will be a gradual rollout before eventually moving on to a normal rollout for all Windows 11 devices once it reaches general availability. The highlight of the new update should calm annoyed users who have spent years with custom scripts and services in an attempt to shape Windows the way they would prefer it. Users will get a "customize menu" button that controls what commands appear when they right-click their mouse. Users can toggle built-in commands such as Send To or Create Shortcut on or off, rearrange what appears on the main menu, and control which third-party extensions show up in either the main or submenus. The gripe with the right-click menu had been that Microsoft hid familiar command locations behind a top row of icons while moving other familiar commands under the "Show more options" submenu. Now, Windows users can customize the whole thing around their habits.

The new preview also highlights a new Windows feature called Cloud Rebuild, a recovery option that can reinstall Windows 11 directly from the cloud, even when an existing Windows 11 fails to boot. Cloud Rebuild will pull the Windows 11 image and needed system drivers directly from Windows Update. Users will not need a custom recovery image or external media to reinstall Windows. There is an important distinction to note, however. Microsoft classifies Cloud Rebuild as a recovery option, but it behaves more like a fresh Windows install than a repair, as existing applications and files will not be included. Those worried about data security can sanitize entire system drives prior to reinstalling. For a full list of improvements coming to Windows 11, including changes to Xbox mode and settings, you can view the official Microsoft release announcement .

PLAYABLE WITH VOICEOVER GemGame plays with VoiceOver. Every gem and obstacle on the board has a clear spoken label, a Board status element counts obstacles and ingredients, and a Special gems element counts specials. Each move is summarised after it settles, including the chain multiplier. Purchased hints name the exact pair to swap, and rejected moves explain why without spending a move. AWAKEN THE FIVE WORLDS Restore the Conservatory's light, reconnect the Nebula Waterways, unfold the Aurora Observatory, illuminate the Plasma Forge and awaken the Heart of the Void. Your campaign progress makes each transformation permanent. Return to choose free lighting, replay the awakening and pursue optional mastery. Choose decorative finishes, discover new districts and welcome butterflies, songbirds and other woodland visitors as you play. Keep your streak going. • Relic Run: draft relics and climb five boards in a single free run. • Weekend Gauntlet: a Friday-to-Sunday sudden-death ladder. en.title: Trump declares robot imports a national security threat
en.summary: President orders trade talks on foreign-made factory robots, threatens tariffs.
en.body:
President Donald Trump has declared the imports of foreign-made factory robots to be a national security threat—ordering new US negotiations with trading partners while holding out the possibility of imposing new tariffs on such robot imports in the future.

Issued on October 28, Trump’s presidential proclamation represents heightened government scrutiny of foreign-made industrial robots that could complicate the manufacturing operations of major US corporations that rely on such robots. Those companies include Detroit automakers General Motors and Ford, electric vehicle manufacturer Tesla , and aerospace and defense giants like Boeing and Lockheed Martin.

Trump’s proclamation describes industrial robots and machinery as being crucial for producing US military weapon systems along with representing a “driving force” behind all critical infrastructure sectors within the US economy. The proclamation cites an investigation under US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick as having found that US imports of such robots “pose[] risks to the United States industrial base and threatens the long-term competitiveness of the United States in a sector that is increasingly vital to national security.”

en.title: Set Up ZoomText and Fusion to Work the Way You Do
en.summary: ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech. In honor of National Disability Employment Awareness Month, our Workplace Ready blog series has run throughout October, …
en.body:
ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech.

In honor of National Disability Employment Awareness Month, our Workplace Ready blog series has run throughout October, with a new post every Thursday spotlighting ZoomText and Fusion features that help you be more productive at work. This is the final post in the series. Last week, we shared practical tips for tackling online tasks. This week, we’ll show you how to set up ZoomText and Fusion to work the way you do.

The features we’ve covered this month are most helpful when they’re tuned to the way you work. Taking a few minutes to customize ZoomText and Fusion is one of the most important steps you can take for workplace productivity. The right magnification level, colors, and view for each task mean less time adjusting settings and more time getting things done.

Personalized settings remove the small points of friction that add up over a busy day. When your tools are ready the moment you open an application, you can move between tasks smoothly and work more efficiently and independently. This week, we’ll look at how to save settings for each application, set up your preferred colors and display options, and use touch screen support on compatible devices.

The settings that work well in one program may not be the best choice for another. With Application Settings, you can save unique magnification and enhancement settings for each application you use. Once saved, ZoomText and Fusion automatically load the right settings as you switch between programs, so you don’t have to stop and adjust your view every time you change tasks.

To create Application Settings, open the application and adjust magnification, cursor, or mouse settings to meet your needs, then open the ZoomText menu, choose Application Settings , and save the current settings for that application. To keep your general preferences for every other program, choose Configurations > Save As Default from the ZoomText menu.

Here’s how this might look across a typical workday:

When you move from writing a report in Word to answering email in Outlook, ZoomText and Fusion switch to your Outlook settings automatically. When you come back, your Word settings are right where you left them.

The right colors can make text easier to read and reduce eye strain over a long workday. Color Enhancements let you choose from a variety of preset color schemes, such as inverted brightness or high-contrast combinations, or create your own custom colors. To pick a scheme, select the arrow next to the Color button on the Magnifier toolbar tab. Press CAPS LOCK+C to toggle color enhancements on and off. When you find a combination you like, save it as part of your default configuration or your Application Settings so it’s ready when you need it.

Different tasks also call for different views. ZoomText and Fusion offer several zoom window types for a single monitor: Full , Overlay , Lens , Line , and Docked (Top, Bottom, Left, or Right). Full magnifies the entire screen, which works well for reading documents. Docked keeps part of the screen at normal size, which can be helpful when you want to see the whole layout of an application while magnifying the area you’re working in. Press CAPS LOCK+Z to cycle through the zoom window types, or select the Window button on the Magnifier toolbar tab to choose one.

If you use more than one monitor, ZoomText and Fusion can extend your workspace across two displays. When your monitors are set to extend your desktop, you can choose from these zoom window types:

In the MultiView modes, press CAPS LOCK+V to switch the active view. For more options, such as keeping both views at the same magnification level, select Window > Settings on the Magnifier toolbar tab and choose Multiple Monitor Options .

If you work on a touch screen laptop or tablet, you can control ZoomText and Fusion with gestures. Touch Screen Support works on Windows devices that support at least five simultaneous touch points.

To get started, open the ZoomText menu and choose Preferences > Touch Screen Support > Enable Touch Icon . The Touch Icon lets you switch between two modes:

Double-tap the Touch Icon with one finger to switch modes. To switch for just a moment, hold one finger on the icon, then lift it to return to the previous mode.

In ZoomText Touch Mode, try these gestures:

A few tips can make touch more comfortable at work. Choose a Touch Icon size and color that are easy for you to see from Preferences > Touch Screen Support on the ZoomText menu. Move the icon out of the way by holding one finger on it and dragging it along the edge of the screen. If you share time between a keyboard and touch, keep the icon in Windows Touch Mode when you’re tapping through applications and switch to ZoomText Touch Mode when you want to zoom or pan.

That brings our Workplace Ready series to a close. Throughout October, we’ve explored how ZoomText and Fusion can help you work more productively and independently. Here’s a look back at what we covered:

There’s always more to discover. Take some time to explore additional features and try new settings as your work changes. For tutorials, webinars, and other learning materials, visit our training page. Thank you for following along this month, and keep thriving in your workplace!

Have questions? Email training@vispero.com .

en.title: Google admits AI search makes less money, but it's fixing that with more ads
en.summary: Google's negative cash flow balloons to -$9.06 billion, and stock price tumbles following Q3 earnings.
en.body:
Google parent Alphabet reported its Q3 financial results on Wednesday afternoon, showing a healthy rise in revenue for the months of July to September. But the company's stock price has taken a beating, marking one of the largest post-earnings drops in its history. It comes down to several troubling aspects of the new report, including an admission by the company that AI search isn't earning as much as organic search, and despite that, Google expects to spend even more on AI next year.

The company took in almost $128 billion in Q3 2026, earning more than $26 billion in net income. These may sound like good numbers, but financial markets are not impressed. While revenue is up 25 percent versus last year, net income is almost $9 billion lower. As of this story's publication, the stock price is down almost 12 percent, and it was down about 13 percent earlier in the day.

While revenue was up 25 percent year over year, analysts expected more. Google reported earnings per share of $2.12, but the consensus projection ahead of Wednesday was $3.02. Google's Cloud products actually beat expectations, crossing $30 billion in revenue. That's about a billion more than analyst guesses.

es.title: Duke investiga una IA en el móvil para mejorar la asistencia visual
es.summary: La inteligencia artificial para personas con discapacidad visual sigue avanzando. Un equipo de investigación vinculado a Duke University, en Estados Unidos, trabaja en un sistema capaz de detectar obstáculos, identificar objetos que se aproximan y describir el entorno mediante indicaciones de audio. El proyecto combina unas gafas con cámara y un teléfono móvil. Su objetivo […] La entrada Duke investiga una IA en el móvil para mejorar la asistencia visual se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
La inteligencia artificial para personas con discapacidad visual sigue avanzando. Un equipo de investigación vinculado a Duke University, en Estados Unidos, trabaja en un sistema capaz de detectar obstáculos, identificar objetos que se aproximan y describir el entorno mediante indicaciones de audio.

El proyecto combina unas gafas con cámara y un teléfono móvil. Su objetivo es facilitar información útil durante los desplazamientos y otras actividades cotidianas.

Además, los investigadores quieren ejecutar el modelo de inteligencia artificial directamente en el teléfono, de esta forma, el sistema podría funcionar sin depender de servidores externos para procesar las imágenes.

La propuesta utiliza gafas inteligentes equipadas con una cámara que captura el entorno de la persona usuaria. Las imágenes se envían al sistema de inteligencia artificial para analizar lo que ocurre alrededor.

A partir de esa información, el sistema busca proporcionar indicaciones de audio sobre posibles peligros y elementos relevantes del entorno.

Entre las funciones que investiga el equipo se encuentran:

Estas funciones pretenden complementar las herramientas de movilidad existentes, como el bastón blanco o el perro guía. No buscan sustituirlas.

Una de las principales líneas de trabajo es conseguir que el sistema procese las imágenes en el propio teléfono, en lugar de enviarlas continuamente a servidores externos.

Para ello, el equipo ha trabajado con un modelo de inteligencia artificial comprimido, denominado modelo de 0,5 mil millones de parámetros. Esta reducción busca que el sistema pueda ejecutarse en un dispositivo móvil con recursos limitados.

Los investigadores han comparado un sistema básico de alertas basado en reglas con este nuevo modelo, diseñado para interpretar mejor el contexto de los posibles peligros.

Sin embargo, el equipo todavía debe completar un paso fundamental: exportar el modelo para que funcione directamente en el dispositivo. Por tanto, la asistencia inteligente sin conexión a internet es un objetivo del proyecto, no una función que deba darse por plenamente disponible.

Ejecutar la inteligencia artificial en el móvil puede ofrecer varias ventajas para las tecnologías de apoyo a la discapacidad visual.

En primer lugar, el sistema podría responder con mayor rapidez al no tener que enviar cada imagen a un servidor remoto y esperar su respuesta. En una situación de desplazamiento, reducir ese tiempo puede ser especialmente importante.

Además, el procesamiento local permitiría reducir la dependencia de una conexión a internet. Esto facilitaría el uso de determinadas funciones en lugares con poca cobertura.

Por último, mantener las imágenes en el propio dispositivo podría mejorar la privacidad, ya que reduciría la necesidad de transmitir vídeos del entorno a servidores externos. No obstante, la protección de los datos también dependerá del funcionamiento completo de la aplicación y de cómo gestione la información.

Estas ventajas son posibilidades técnicas que deberán comprobarse mediante pruebas del sistema terminado.

Aunque la investigación abre nuevas posibilidades, todavía es necesario evaluar el funcionamiento del sistema en condiciones reales.

Por ejemplo, detectar un obstáculo en una imagen no garantiza que se identifique correctamente durante un desplazamiento. Los cambios de iluminación, los espacios concurridos y los objetos difíciles de distinguir pueden afectar a los resultados.

También será importante comprobar la rapidez de las alertas, la autonomía de la batería y la facilidad de uso de las gafas. Además, los avisos deberán ser claros y oportunos para no sobrecargar de información sonora a la persona usuaria.

Por ello, las pruebas con personas ciegas y con baja visión serán fundamentales para determinar si esta tecnología aporta beneficios reales en la vida cotidiana.

La investigación de Duke University refleja una tendencia creciente en tiflotecnología: desarrollar sistemas de inteligencia artificial más pequeños y capaces de funcionar en dispositivos portátiles.

Si se consigue ejecutar el modelo directamente en el móvil, la propuesta podría reducir la dependencia de internet y facilitar respuestas más inmediatas sobre el entorno.

Aun así, el proyecto sigue en desarrollo y todavía debe demostrar su eficacia en situaciones reales. Su evolución permitirá conocer hasta qué punto la inteligencia artificial local puede complementar las ayudas de movilidad y contribuir a la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual.

Fuentes: Duke University, Rhodes Information Initiative — Data+: AI-Powered Hazard Detection for the Visually Impaired (22 de julio de 2026)

en.title: Apple Introduces Updated iMac and MacBook Pros with Performance and Connectivity Improvements, a Touchscreen for the High-End MacBook Pro, and More
en.summary: On the heels of introducing the 8th generation iPad Mini , Apple this week updated the iMac and MacBook Pro, bringing faster chips, improved connectivity, and, for the first time, a touchscreen to the MacBook Pro. iMac Featuring up to a 12-core CPU, the new iMac with M6, according to Apple's press release , delivers: Up to 2.5x faster performance in apps like Microsoft Excel, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 1.5x faster performance than M4. Up to 3.3x faster graphics performance for tasks including photo editing in Affinity, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 2x faster performance than M4. Up to 12x faster on-device AI performance for prompt processing in LM Studio, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 5x faster performance than M4. Up to 2x higher gaming performance with ray tracing compared to M4. Up to 2x faster SSD read and write performance. With the N1 wireless networking chip, the new iMac supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and up to a 2.5 gigabit Ethernet port, included with the power adapter. The iMac with M6 is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the stand, 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards, and is manufactured with 40 percent renewable electricity. It can be pre-ordered from Apple in green, yellow, orange, pink, purple, blue, and silver starting today for a starting price of US $1499, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6. MacBook Pro In addition to the iMac, Apple updated the base 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, N1 wireless networking chip, and up to 170 GBPS of unified memory bandwidth. The MacBook Pro with M6, according to Apple's press release delivers: Up to 13x faster time to first token performance for LLM prompt processing compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 11.7x faster render performance with ray tracing in Blender compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 3.3x faster image-processing performance in Affinity compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.2x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 2.5x faster project build performance when compiling code in Xcode compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Apple also claims the 12-core GPU paired with the dual 16-core neural engine features up to 30 percent faster graphics performance compared to M5, as well as up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads. The new MacBook Pro also features the N1 wireless networking chip, bringing Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support. The MacBook Pro with M6 is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors, and is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity across the supply chain. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for a starting price of US $1999, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6. Apple has also introduced new high-end 14 and 16-inch MacBook Pros , bringing a thinner and lighter design, a redesigned thermal architecture, a new speaker design, hinge improvements, and, for the first time on a Mac, an OLED touchscreen and Dynamic Island. With the Dynamic Island, users will be able to view Live Activities, answer calls, and use Siri and Spotlight. At the time of publication, we do not know how VoiceOver or any other macOS accessibility tool will work with touch controls. The MacBook Pro with PROOLEDXDR display continues to use the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, but it now features a redesigned thermal architecture that Apple claims better redirects air away from the display, helping to prevent it from getting warm to the touch while maintaining sustained performance. The MacBook Pro with PROOLEDXDR display is made with 55 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors, and is manufactured with 45 percent renewable electricity across the supply chain. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for a starting price of US $2899, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6.

en.title: Real world
en.summary: Welcome to Real World, created by NBM Studios! In this game, players are thrust into a 3D world full of danger and excitement. As a…
en.body:
Published 28 October 2026 by Nr Witta Draco

Welcome to Real World , created by NBM Studios! In this game, players are thrust into a 3D world full of danger and excitement. As a blind player, you must rely on your other senses and quick reflexes to navigate the environment and take down your enemies.

With a variety of weapons at your disposal, including wands for casting spells, you can hunt other players and animals, as well as dragons. If you are lucky enough to defeat the fearsome dragon, you will be rewarded with valuable items and TL, the in-game currency. But beware: the dragon respawns after 30 minutes, giving other players the chance to challenge it.

In addition to intense player-vs-player combat, the game also offers a variety of missions and challenges to complete. You can rob banks and palaces, steal valuable items, and earn extra TL. You can also take on mafia missions and defeat gangsters to earn even more rewards. As you progress through the game, you can even purchase your own hotel and use it as a base of operations. With a dynamic and constantly changing world, no two games are ever the same.

The adventure does not stop there. In Real World, players can also team up with friends and form clans to take on even more challenging missions and quests. For players who want to take their gameplay further, the game also offers a range of paid items and paid accounts that can provide additional advantages in battle.

You can create tickets to request new features or report bugs, and even marry other players if you choose. Whether you prefer to go it alone or fight alongside your clan, the choice is yours. Join the adventure and see if you have what it takes to survive in this thrilling game for blind players!

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Real world is an audio-based game designed with accessibility in mind. It includes a built-in screen reader, so TalkBack is not required while playing.

You can explore different maps, purchase weapons and other items from the in-game store using the game’s currency, and discover different areas featuring animals and other elements.

The app’s user interface is accessible, with no unlabeled buttons reported. The game is easy to use once you learn its touchscreen gestures.

en.title: Announcing AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month for October 2026: ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App
en.summary: Welcome to the October 2026 installment of AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month, where each month I highlight a new or noteworthy app. This month's pick is ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App, a fun and relaxing water-sorting puzzle game that has quickly become one of my favorites. I know, I know. Another game for my App Pick of the Month! I realize not everyone here is a gamer, and I'm sorry for picking yet another one. But we've had so many fun new games coming our way lately, I just can't help myself! ReSort was simply too much fun to pass up. Maybe next month I'll pick something different. No promises, though! About ReSort ReSort is a puzzle game where you sort different-colored water into separate tubes until each tube contains just one color. Sounds simple enough, right? Well, it starts out that way, but things get trickier as you progress. Before long, you're moving water back and forth, trying to figure out your next move without getting yourself stuck. What I really enjoy is that there's no rush with ReSort. No timers, no move limits, and no pressure. You can take your time and figure things out at your own pace. But don't mistake relaxing for easy! Some puzzles can really get you scratching your head, and finally solving one that's been giving you trouble is incredibly satisfying. There's plenty to keep you busy, too. Along with the regular levels, ReSort offers daily puzzles with different difficulty settings and a larger Sunday challenge. You can also earn stars, work your way through different ranks, and unlock additional sounds as you progress. Accessibility is another reason ReSort stands out. The game was designed with VoiceOver in mind, with announcements for the colors and their positions in each tube. And I have to say, I absolutely love the sounds in this game! From the satisfying sound of pouring water to the little audio cues and gentle music, everything adds to the experience. It's one of those games where the sounds make playing that much more enjoyable. I also love that you can customize them to your liking. Something else I really appreciate is the developer's involvement with the AppleVis community. Since introducing ReSort in the AppleVis forum , the developer has been actively listening to feedback and making improvements. Suggestions from community members have already led to different daily puzzle difficulties, iCloud syncing, more sound options, and adjustable tube sizes for low-vision players. I love seeing developers take our community's suggestions seriously, especially when those suggestions turn into actual features so quickly. It's wonderful to see that kind of engagement. Why I'm Picking ReSort This Month For me, ReSort is just plain fun. It's easy to learn, challenging enough to keep me interested, and relaxing enough to enjoy whenever I have a few minutes to spare. And that's where the trouble starts! I'll tell myself I'm only going to play a couple of levels, and before I know it, I've played several more. There's always another puzzle waiting, and I can't seem to resist finding out whether I can solve it. I also appreciate getting to enjoy this type of game with VoiceOver. Water-sorting games have been around for years, but finding one that's this accessible isn't something I take for granted. Between the enjoyable gameplay, wonderful sounds, thoughtful accessibility, and a developer who's genuinely listening to our community, ReSort has earned its place as my October App Pick of the Month. If you enjoy puzzle games, or just want something relaxing that gives your brain a little workout, I definitely recommend giving ReSort a try. Just don't blame me if you find yourself playing longer than you planned! Download the App ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App is available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad. The first 10 levels are free, with a one-time purchase to unlock the remaining levels. There are no ads or subscriptions, and all accessibility features are included for free. Now It's Your Turn Have you tried ReSort yet? Are you finding it as addictive as I am? How far have you made it in the game? I'd love to hear what you think and what other apps or games you've been enjoying this month. Let me know in the comments. I always enjoy hearing what everyone else is playing and discovering!

es.title: TDK desarrolla un espejo ultrafino para proyectar imágenes directamente en la retina
es.summary: La empresa tecnológica TDK ha presentado un sistema que utiliza un espejo metaóptico de apenas 150 nanómetros de grosor para dirigir imágenes hacia la retina. Esta tecnología podría facilitar el desarrollo de gafas inteligentes más discretas y ligeras. El avance se dirige al mercado de las gafas inteligentes y la realidad aumentada. Además, abre nuevas […] La entrada TDK desarrolla un espejo ultrafino para proyectar imágenes directamente en la retina se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
La empresa tecnológica TDK ha presentado un sistema que utiliza un espejo metaóptico de apenas 150 nanómetros de grosor para dirigir imágenes hacia la retina. Esta tecnología podría facilitar el desarrollo de gafas inteligentes más discretas y ligeras.

El avance se dirige al mercado de las gafas inteligentes y la realidad aumentada. Además, abre nuevas posibilidades para investigar futuras aplicaciones de la tiflotecnología. Sin embargo, todavía no es una ayuda visual disponible para personas con baja visión.

Los sistemas de proyección retinal dirigen haces de luz hacia la retina para generar una imagen que percibe la persona que lleva el dispositivo. De esta forma, pueden mostrar información digital sin depender exclusivamente de una pantalla convencional situada delante de los ojos.

Hasta ahora, uno de los retos de esta tecnología era el tamaño de sus componentes ópticos. Algunos sistemas necesitan espejos curvos voluminosos cerca de los ojos, lo que dificulta conseguir unas gafas con una apariencia similar a la de unas gafas convencionales.

Para resolver este problema, TDK ha desarrollado un espejo metaóptico que utiliza estructuras a escala nanométrica para controlar la reflexión de la luz. Su diseño permite integrar el componente directamente en una lente, en lugar de utilizar un espejo curvo de mayor tamaño.

El nuevo componente presentado por TDK destaca por sus dimensiones y transparencia. Según los datos publicados por la empresa, sus principales características son:

Además, el diseño pretende reducir la visibilidad de las imágenes proyectadas desde el exterior. Así, otras personas no deberían ver el contenido digital que recibe quien lleva las gafas.

Los resultados técnicos también se han recogido en un artículo publicado en SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers en septiembre de 2026. El trabajo describe la integración del espejo metaóptico en una lente y un sistema de visualización con resolución de 1.280 × 720 píxeles y un campo de visión diagonal de 45 grados.

La investigación sobre proyección retinal puede resultar relevante para el desarrollo de futuras ayudas visuales. Unas gafas con componentes ópticos más pequeños podrían facilitar la integración de información digital sin recurrir a estructuras voluminosas.

En el ámbito de la discapacidad visual, estas tecnologías podrían investigarse para mostrar información contextual, indicaciones de navegación o elementos de realidad aumentada. También podrían combinarse en el futuro con sistemas de inteligencia artificial capaces de describir el entorno o proporcionar información mediante audio.

No obstante, es importante distinguir entre las posibilidades de una tecnología y sus aplicaciones demostradas. TDK ha presentado un avance en el sistema óptico de las gafas, pero no ha demostrado que este desarrollo mejore la autonomía de personas con baja visión en situaciones cotidianas.

La utilidad para cada persona dependerá, entre otros factores, de sus necesidades visuales, las características de la imagen, el contraste, el brillo y la facilidad de uso del dispositivo completo.

Por el momento, el desarrollo de TDK se encuentra en fase de demostración tecnológica. La empresa trabaja para conseguir una versión a todo color y avanzar hacia la fabricación en serie durante los próximos años.

Por tanto, todavía no se puede hablar de un producto comercial de ayuda visual ni confirmar su precio, disponibilidad en España o utilidad clínica. También será necesario conocer las prestaciones del dispositivo completo y evaluar aspectos como la seguridad ocular, la autonomía y el funcionamiento en diferentes condiciones de iluminación.

El espejo metaóptico de TDK representa un avance en la miniaturización de los sistemas ópticos para gafas inteligentes. Su integración en una lente transparente podría ayudar a superar algunas de las barreras de diseño que han limitado el desarrollo de estos dispositivos.

Para la tiflotecnología, el interés está en comprobar si futuros sistemas basados en esta tecnología pueden ofrecer funciones realmente útiles y accesibles para las personas con discapacidad visual.

Desde EsRetina seguiremos atentos a la evolución de estas investigaciones y a las novedades que puedan traducirse en soluciones prácticas para mejorar la accesibilidad y la autonomía personal.

Fuentes: TDK: comunicado oficial sobre el sistema de proyección retinal (2 de octubre de 2026) , Mizuno y colaboradores: Direct Retinal Projection by Meta-Optic Mirror for Smart Glasses , SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers (2026) , TDK: explicación técnica del espejo metaóptico

en.title: Apple Introduces Updated iPad Mini with Thinner and Lighter Design, Upgraded Display and Camera, A20 Pro chip, N1 and C2 Networking Chips, and More
en.summary: Apple today introduced the new 8th-generation iPad mini, bringing a thinner and lighter design, an 8.5-inch OLED display, A20 Pro chip, N1 and C2 networking chips, a new audio system, and more. With the new design, iPad mini features an upgraded 8.5-inch OLED display while maintaining its existing footprint, thanks to 24 percent thinner bezels. A new audio system that integrates components between the display and enclosure removes the speaker holes and contributes to an IP67 water and dust resistance rating, a first for any iPad. With A20 Pro, Apple claims iPad mini delivers up to 4.5X faster AI performance, up to 2.7X faster graphics performance, and up to 60 percent faster performance for everyday tasks compared to the previous generation. In addition, the N1 wireless networking chip adds Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support to iPad mini, and cellular models of the device include Apple's C2 modem, which Apple claims delivers up to 50 percent faster data speeds compared to the previous generation. The 12MP Center Stage front camera has been moved to the landscape edge of the device, as it is on other iPad models. Apple touts this as beneficial for FaceTime calls and collaboration. Apple additionally claims that the new Adaptive True Tone flash improves photos and document scanning. To compliment the new iPad mini, Apple has also introduced a new Smart Folio magnetic cover that features "TechWoven" fabric. The new iPad mini is made with 35 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and is manufactured with 40 percent renewable energy across the supply chain. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting Wednesday, October 28 in midnight and starlight finishes for a starting price of US $699, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6.

en.title: Apple Releases iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 with Expanded Language Support for Siri AI, Profiles for the TV App, Bug Fixes, and More
en.summary: Apple has today released iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 to the public, bringing Siri AI support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, support for multiple profiles in the TV app, anniversary alerts in Call Context, and various bug fixes. Apple has also released iOS 26.7.2 for devices not running iOS 27. Resolved Accessibility Bugs Our experience is that the following accessibility bugs have been resolved or meaningfully improved in iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2: The changes made to VoiceOver's audio profile in iOS 27.0 and iPadOS 27.0 appear to have been reverted. Using the Dot Pad, The f1 and f4 keys now pan the larger 20x8 display correctly. Also using the Dot Pad, the triangular-shaped buttons now pan the 20-cell display as expected. The gesture, keyboard shortcut, and Perkins-style keyboard commands for Touch and Sound Curtain once again work as expected. Navigating and selecting text with a hardware keyboard is significantly improved. VoiceOver recognizing and speaking when an item state changes or when information has updated is significantly improved, however, the issue may still occur occasionally. The buttons to switch between All and Missed in the Phone app's Classic view, as well as the ones to switch between Start Page, Bookmarks, Reading List, and History in Safari, now work. The "Clear All" rotor action in Notification Center once again works. The "Direct Touch" option in VoiceOver's Quick Settings panel once again works. It is once again possible to swipe from the battery indicator to other items on the status bar when an app is opened. VoiceOver's "copy to clipboard" function now only copies the desired content rather than the full semantic markup. The Call button on the keypad in the Phone app is once again labeled correctly. The "Delete" action in the rotor for conversations in the Siri app is no longer doubled. It is no longer necessary to remove the previously-assigned command in VoiceOver Settings before a new one will work. VoiceOver once again speaks the time at the top of the hour correctly when in 24 hour mode. The "Show Bookmarks" button is once again labeled correctly when the Safari toolbar is set to "Bottom." VoiceOver now works in the "Device Diagnostics" option in the Recovery Menu. The VoiceOver per-voice equalizer now works as expected. VoiceOver once again behaves as expected when editing text and placing focus on a combo box. The Camera App no longer contains extraneous UI elements for editing camera controls when Edit Mode is not active. When swiping through the Lock Screen, VoiceOver focus once again behaves in a consistent and predictable way. In the Camera App, the VoiceOver boundary behavior now works as expected when reaching the first or last element onscreen. New Accessibility Bugs We are currently aware of two new accessibility bugs in these releases: When encountering some emojis and some pictorial icons, VoiceOver speaks them as the words "unspeakable English text." Examples of how this issue may present include: In WhatsApp, you may have a family group name which includes an emoji of adults and children holding hands. Instead of hearing "Family, man, woman and child holding hands emoji", you hear "Family, unspeakable English text". On a website, an icon with a shopping cart may say "Unspeakable English text" instead of "Shopping cart". When navigating content, VoiceOver will on occasion stop speaking, and only provide sounds and haptic feedback. This typically lasts for 20 to 30 seconds. If you notice any further changes, improvements, or regressions in your use of these releases, please post a comment below with your findings. Release Notes iOS 27.2 This update provides enhancements to Siri AI with the ability to retain useful context from previous Siri interactions as well as draw from a wider range of personal context. It also introduces Suggestions in Messages that help you take quick actions in apps like Calendar and Reminders based on context from your conversation. This release includes additional features, bug fixes, and security updates for your iPhone. Siri AI (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) Siri AI can recall your past conversations, so you can ask Siri about something it told you before, like the restaurants it recommended last week. Siri AI can draw from more sources to give you a great answer, including photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, your voicemails, and better results from Safari history and Reading List. Excluded Apps lets you choose which apps Siri, Search, and suggestions can access, all from one setting. Granular text selection lets you select and copy just the part of a Siri response you need. Siri AI is available in more languages, with support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. Siri AI is not available in the EU or mainland China. Other Suggestions in Messages help you take action based on the context of your conversations, like adding a Calendar invite for a dinner. Shared Albums in Photos adds the ability to edit captions and comments, to avoid adding duplicate photos, and can display a reminder before albums expire so participants can save important photos and videos. Support for SynthID watermarking to help identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground. The Home tab in the Podcasts app offers two separate sections for New Episodes and Continue Playing, letting you find the latest updates from your shows and then pick up where you left off. Friends tab in the Games app provides context on friend suggestions and shows recent games played on friends’ player pages. Simple Profiles in the Apple TV app lets everyone in your household have their own profile, with recommendations that fit what they like to watch. FaceTime supports adding a third party sign language interpreter or live captioner to a call. To learn more, please visit: https://support.apple.com/125039 How to Update iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 are available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update), via Finder on a Mac with macOS Catalina or later, or via iTunes on a PC or Mac with macOS Mojave or earlier. Before updating, we strongly recommend making a full and complete backup of your device (either locally or in iCloud, depending on personal preference). This will ensure that, in the unlikely event that something goes wrong during the update process, you will have a current backup on hand in case a device restore becomes necessary. Also, if using OTA update, we recommend plugging your device into a power source for the duration of the download/installation process, so as to prevent the unlikely event of your battery going dead during the update.

en.title: Apple Releases Version 27.2 of macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and HomePod Software

Our experience is that the following accessibility bug has been resolved in macOS Golden Gate 27.2: VoiceOver no longer announces "System has new window" when playing media. We are additionally aware of two new bugs in this release: When navigating an expanded conversation in the messages table in Mail with the up and down arrow keys, VoiceOver speaks “label.text.blank” before each message. When Tabbing past the subject field in Mail’s “New Message” window, focus jumps to the “Format” radio button in the toolbar instead of the next focusable element in the window, requiring you to press the Tab key several additional times to get to the message body text field. If you notice any further changes, improvements, or regressions in your use of these releases, please post a comment below with your findings. It also introduces Suggestions in Messages that help you take quick actions in apps like Calendar and Reminders based on context from your conversation. This release includes additional features, bug fixes, and security updates for your Mac. Siri AI Siri AI can recall your past conversations, so you can ask Siri about something it told you before, like the restaurants it recommended last week. Siri AI can draw from more sources to give you a great answer, including photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, your voicemails, and better results from Safari history and Reading List. Excluded Apps lets you choose which apps Siri, Search, and suggestions can access, all from one setting. Write with Siri is available right from the new formatting bar when you compose a message in Mail. Siri AI is available in more languages, with support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. Siri AI is not available in mainland China. Other Suggestions in Messages help you take action based on the context of your conversations, like adding a Calendar invite for a dinner. Shared Albums in Photos adds the ability to edit captions and comments and avoid adding duplicate photos, and it can display a reminder before albums expire so participants can save important photos and videos. Support for SynthID watermarking to help identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground. The Home tab in the Podcasts app offers two separate sections for New Episodes and Continue Playing, letting you find the latest updates from your shows and then pick up where you left off. FaceTime supports adding a third-party sign-language interpreter or live captioner to a call. watchOS 27.2 This update provides enhancements to Siri AI, including the ability to retain useful context from previous Siri interactions, draw from a wider range of personal context, and deliver faster responses on your watch. This update also includes other features, bug fixes, and security updates for your Apple Watch. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/apple-intelligence Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and/or battery life. To learn more, please visit: https://support.apple.com/125039 tvOS 27.2 This update brings new ways to stay connected with FaceTime, personalize your screen saver, and locate your Siri Remote with Find My, along with bug fixes and security updates for your Apple TV 4K. FaceTime FaceTime links make it easier to join calls directly from your Apple TV. Sign language interpreter and captioning support lets you add third-party services to your calls. Screen Savers Photo personalization lets you use your iPhone to choose specific photos for your screen saver without sharing your full library with Apple TV. Shuffle option lets you enjoy different screen saver categories as your Apple TV cycles through them. Find My Find My support lets you locate your Siri Remote (2nd generation) or later using your iPhone. HomePod Software 27.2 HomePod software version 27.2 brings the new Sound Glow visual experience, home theater surround sound with Apple TV 4K (4th generation), and support for using HomePod speakers with your Mac, along with bug fixes and security updates for your HomePod. Sound Glow on HomePod mini, HomePod mini 2, and HomePod (2nd generation) turns the top of HomePod into a visual display that pulses and glows in sync with your media and shows matching light animations for soundscapes. Home theater surround sound supports connecting four HomePod speakers to Apple TV 4K (4th generation) for an immersive listening experience. Requires matching front and rear pairs of HomePod mini 2 or HomePod (2nd generation). HomePod speakers with your Mac lets you set HomePod as the audio output for everything you do on your Mac, with a responsive and persistent AirPlay connection. Lock controls let you disable the touch controls on top of HomePod to prevent accidental taps from pausing music, skipping songs, or changing the volume. How to Update To install macOS Golden Gate 27.2, choose System Settings from the Apple menu, select General in the table, click Software Update in the scroll area, and click the Update Now button to begin the update process. If other updates are available, you can click the Info button to see details about them and select specific updates to install. watchOS 27.2 is available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update) or by going to the Watch app on your iPhone and navigating to General > Software Update. To install the update, your Watch must be connected to its charger and have at least 50% battery power. To install tvOS 27.2, on Apple TV 4K or Apple TV HD, go to the Settings channel, then look for the System section near the bottom. From here, look for Software Updates under Maintenance, then select Update Software and Download and Install. Wait for your Apple TV to download the update. Don't disconnect or unplug your Apple TV until the update completes. By default, HomePod and HomePod mini automatically install new software updates, but you can manually check for updates in the Home app on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

es.summary: Tras 6 versiones beta y una candidata a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.3, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tras 6 versiones beta y una candidata a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.3, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también en entornos de producción.

Esta versión incluye importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los cuadros de diálogo de NVDA y una mayor compatibilidad con la entrada mediante pantalla táctil. Se han introducido varias mejoras de rendimiento para reducir el retraso y mejorar la capacidad de respuesta. NVDA ahora recopila y almacena en caché más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, lo que mejora el rendimiento en controles como los cuadros combinados y el Explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no provoca que el Explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones se cuelguen al salir de NVDA o al reiniciarlo. Ahora, NVDA se recupera más rápidamente cuando una aplicación deja de responder y ya no se bloquea ni satura el registro con errores de las aplicaciones que no responden. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los cuadros de diálogo «Perfiles de configuración», «Gestos de entrada» y «Diccionarios del habla», lo que facilita el uso de estos cuadros de diálogo con el teclado. Ahora también es posible modificar un gesto ya existente directamente en el cuadro de diálogo «Gestos de entrada». Se ha actualizado el cuadro de diálogo que se utiliza para mostrar los mensajes que se pueden consultar y ahora permite cambiar el tamaño, maximizar y minimizar con mayor facilidad. Se han ampliado considerablemente las opciones de introducción de datos mediante pantalla táctil. Los gestos secuenciales de dos flicks combinan ahora dos flicks consecutivos en un único gesto, lo que aumenta considerablemente el número de gestos táctiles a los que se pueden asignar acciones. Ahora también se admiten los gestos desde los bordes, lo que permite asociar gestos que se inician desde cualquier borde de la pantalla de forma independiente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para desplazar el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Ahora es posible utilizar el OCR de Windows mientras están activos la Cortina de pantalla o el magnificador integrado de NVDA. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas de braille en elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado neozelandés, criollo haitiano, una tabla noruega para texto en español y variantes adicionales suecas de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado eSpeak NG para que sea compatible con el ligur y el abjasio. Consulta todas las novedades aquí Tan pronto como actualices NVDA, no olvides reiniciar el equipo. El reinicio garantiza que se pueden actualizar archivos que antes no se podían modificar porque estaban abiertos para escritura. En la práctica, al reiniciar vuelven a funcionar aplicaciones basadas en Electron, tales como Teams, Dropbox o Google Drive, y dejan de producirse comportamientos extraños con el explorador de archivos, Thunderbird, Office y algunos navegadores. Reiniciar es lo primero que debes hacer antes de informar de cualquier fallo. Hazlo pulsando windows+d para ir al escritorio, alt+f4, e intro sobre la opción Reiniciar. Puedes descargar NVDA 2026.3, así como las últimas versiones compatibles con sistemas antiguos y material útil para desarrolladores, desde nuestra página de descargas . La suma SHA256 de NVDA 2026.3, que se usa para garantizar la integridad de la descarga, es a8a87cb823da0c62cfbae4a444ae5ae238d54dc82ad6d46d3fdb3fef082799b2. Si tienes una versión estable anterior, también puedes actualizar automáticamente desde el menú Ayuda. Y desde la rc1, con el complemento Selector del canal de actualización, se puede hacer del mismo modo configurando previamente el canal estable. Si todavía no conoces NVDA y quieres leer algo más sobre él antes de probarlo, te recomendamos consultar la guía de usuario y la referencia rápida de órdenes . Si te gustan nuestros proyectos y el contenido que ofrecemos, plantéate contribuir mensualmente con una pequeña cantidad. Tan sólo un euro es capaz de marcar la diferencia y ayudarnos a mejorar. Visita la página de donaciones para obtener más información, o la tienda para hacerte con libros de formación traducidos y sintetizadores de voz de alta calidad. ¡Feliz lunes!
