en.title: Access More Online with ZoomText and Fusion
en.summary: ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech. Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful …
en.body:
ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech.

Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful features of ZoomText and Fusion that will help you be more productive in the workplace. This blog series will run throughout October, with a new post every Thursday featuring helpful information and practical tips to make the most of ZoomText and Fusion as you work. Last week, we followed a typical workday from Word to Teams. This week, we’ll provide practical tips for using ZoomText and Fusion when tackling online tasks.

So much of today’s work happens in a web browser: company intranets, online forms, dashboards, and web-based apps for everything from timesheets to project tracking. Whether you’re researching a topic, filling out a form, or checking the latest numbers, having ZoomText or Fusion set up to support the way you browse can make all the difference. This week, we’ll look at how these tools can help you move around websites, find information quickly, read web content comfortably, and keep an eye on the details you check most often.

Busy web pages are easier to work with when you can see exactly where you are. With ZoomText and Fusion, you can quickly adjust your magnification level or switch between different zoom window types, like Lens or Line view, to focus on the part of the page that matters most. Lens and Line are available when you use a single monitor. Lens works like a magnifying glass. It displays a magnified rectangle that follows the mouse pointer. Line works like a magnifying ruler. It displays a magnified horizontal strip that moves up and down the screen and enlarges whatever is directly beneath it.

Press CAPS LOCK+Z to cycle through the available zoom window types until you reach the one you want.

Focus enhancements highlight the item you are on as you navigate using the Tab and arrow keys through links, buttons, and form fields, making it easy to keep your place even at high magnification. Press CAPS LOCK+F to toggle focus enhancements on and off. You can also customize the appearance of the focus locator to suit your needs.

Fusion users can take advantage of the JAWS Virtual Cursor, which simulates a system cursor and lets you read and move through a web page the same way you would a document. The Virtual Cursor is on by default when you are on a web page.

Quick Navigation keys let you jump straight to the content you need without scanning the entire page. Press H to move to the next heading, F to move to the next form field, and L to move to the next list. Add SHIFT to any of these keys, such as SHIFT+H , to move backward. Press TAB to move through links and form controls.

Long pages and crowded web apps can hide the information you are trying to locate. The ZoomText Finder tool lets you search for words or phrases on web pages and in documents. Open Finder from the ZoomText toolbar, type your search term, and use the navigation buttons to jump between results. ZoomText brings each match into the magnified view, so you don’t have to pan around the page looking for it.

Fusion users can use the Find command to locate specific text on a web page. Press CTRL+F to open the Find dialog, type your search term, and press ENTER to jump to the next occurrence. Press F3 to navigate to the next occurrence of that text.

For even faster navigation, JAWS can list every link or heading on a page. Press CAPS LOCK+F7 to open the Links List or CAPS LOCK+F6 to open the Headings List, then choose an item and press ENTER to jump directly to the section or link you need.

Articles, reports, and long web pages are easier to get through when you don’t have to read every word on screen. AppReader reads documents, web pages, and email aloud while you follow along or rest your eyes. It can read from beginning to end, skim forward and backward, or read just the text you select with the mouse. AppReader reads text aloud in three modes: App View reads directly in the source application without changing your view, Text View reformats the text with your choice of fonts, colors, and magnification for easier reading, and the SpeakIt Tool reads any text on the screen that you select by clicking and dragging. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+A to launch App View. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+T to launch Text View. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+S to launch the SpeakIt Tool.

To start reading at a specific word on a web page, point to it with the mouse and press CAPS LOCK+ALT+LEFT-CLICK . Text View is especially helpful on cluttered pages, since it strips away the layout and shows just the text in a format that’s comfortable for you.

Background Reader in ZoomText lets you listen to web content while you keep working on other tasks. Select and copy the text you want to hear, then press CAPS LOCK+CTRL+B to start Background Reader. You can continue working in other applications while the content is read aloud.

Fusion users can use the JAWS Say All command to read an entire article from the cursor position. Press CAPS LOCK+DOWN ARROW to start continuous reading, and press CTRL to stop. This is perfect for reviewing long articles or reports.

Many of us return to the same web pages and apps every day to check a status, a total, or a notification. Reading Zones put that information one keystroke away. A reading zone is a defined area of an application window that ZoomText can display, speak, or both, at the press of a hotkey. You can set up as many as 10 zones.

To create a reading zone, open the web page or application, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+C , then drag a rectangle over the area you want the zone to cover. Give the zone a name and choose whether it should be displayed, spoken, or both.

To trigger a reading zone, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+ the zone’s number (1 through 9, or 0 for zone 10). Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+N to move to the next zone and CAPS LOCK+ALT+P to move to the previous zone, or press CAPS LOCK+ALT+L to list all your zones.

For example, if you regularly check a dashboard with multiple widgets, set up Reading Zones for the most important ones. With a single keystroke, ZoomText can magnify or speak the data you need, without searching the page for it.

Join us next week as we explore how to set up ZoomText and Fusion to work the way you do, customizing settings for your workflow, preferences, and productivity. Stay tuned for more tips to help you thrive in your workplace!

Have questions? Email training@vispero.com .

La inteligencia artificial puede ayudarnos a crear documentos PDF de forma más sencilla y adaptada a nuestras necesidades. En la próxima Jornada de Actualización de Desarrollos y Avances Tecnológicos , aprenderemos cómo utilizar estas herramientas y qué instrucciones debemos darles para obtener los resultados que buscamos.

La sesión tendrá lugar el martes 27 de octubre, a partir de las 11:00 horas , y será impartida por Iván García. La actividad se desarrollará en línea, a través de Jitsi Meeten: https://meet.jit.si/Saladegrupo

Durante la sesión, conoceremos cómo generar documentos PDF utilizando herramientas de inteligencia artificial. También veremos qué pautas debemos seguir para orientar correctamente el proceso y conseguir documentos que respondan a una tarea específica.

Uno de los aspectos principales será el uso de prompts , es decir, las instrucciones que proporcionamos a la inteligencia artificial para indicarle qué necesitamos. Aprenderemos cómo redactarlos y qué información debemos incluir para obtener resultados más precisos y útiles.

Esta jornada será una oportunidad para descubrir nuevas posibilidades de la inteligencia artificial y conocer recursos que pueden facilitarnos las tareas cotidianas.

¡Os animamos a participar y a seguir descubriendo las posibilidades que nos ofrecen los avances tecnológicos!

en.title: Oath & Ash
en.summary: Oath & Ash (Eid & Asche) is a turn-based fantasy card game with detailed art, animated hero portraits and punchy battle sound. It is fully playable with VoiceOver. Every card, every enemy move and every result is announced, and nothing is ever timed. THREE HEROES, THREE WAYS TO PLAY The Knight holds the line with armor, guard and counterattacks. The Hunter sets traps, spreads poison and outlasts the enemy. The Mage controls the flow of cards with chains and frost. The Hunter unlocks after Act I, the Mage after Act II. Each hero has their own cards, deck and progress. THREE ACTS Walk the Thorn Path, cross the Ashlands and brave the Sand Sea. Each act has ten encounters, its own enemies and boss fights. Enemies show their next move before they make it, so you can plan ahead. Losing costs you no progress. Change your deck and try again. COLLECT AND UPGRADE Win cards in battle or open card boxes with three random cards. The app shows the odds for each rarity before you open a box. Salvage duplicates for Dust and use it to upgrade your favorite cards. Your deck is yours to build. SOMETHING NEW EVERY DAY Check the Daily tab for a new challenge each day, with its own rules and rewards. EXPEDITIONS Set out with a small deck and build it as you go. Three legs, each a map with branching paths to fights, rests, merchants and events, and a boss at the end. Relics give you lasting advantages, and your health carries over from fight to fight. In the weekly Expedition everyone plays the same map, and the top places in the ranking win weekly prizes. THE SEASON PATH Wins, duels and daily battles earn you embers to climb the Season Path: 40 levels of Dust, Diamonds, card boxes, titles, card backs, frames, avatars and victory lines. New looks arrive every month. The Path Letter opens a second track with more rewards. THE ARENA Duel the saved defense decks of real players. You play your turns, the game plays theirs. There is no turn timer, and every deck fights with its real card levels, so deckbuilding and tactics decide. If no player is a good match, a clearly labeled Arena Guardian steps in for half points. Climb from Starter through Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum to Diamond. Each season lasts one month, and the ranking shows your display name and avatar. Challenge friends to friendly duels with an invite link, and every profile shows league, heroes and collection. BUILT FOR VOICEOVER • Every value, card text and enemy intent is spoken • No time pressure, in the acts or in the Arena • Battle log with one heading per round for quick navigation • Narrator Helmut guides you in English and German • Every enemy has a voice of its own, and every boss its own music and entrance • You can hear when it's your turn, how hard a hit landed and when your health runs low • Settings, Learn the sounds lets you hear every sound and what it means • Support for larger text, reduced motion and haptic feedback GOOD TO KNOW Your progress is saved to your iCloud account, so you need to be signed in to iCloud on your device. Battles, Expeditions and the Arena need an internet connection. Your collection and the tutorial also work offline. Diamonds and the Path Letter are optional in-app purchases. There are no ads. Questions or problems? Reach us at support.kroegoor.com.

es.title: Las Ray-Ban Meta llegan a los museos para acercar el arte a las personas ciegas y con baja visión
es.summary: La Pinacoteca de Brera, en Milán, ha puesto en marcha Sensing Art, un proyecto piloto que combina gafas inteligentes, audiodescripción e inteligencia artificial para facilitar una visita más autónoma a las personas con discapacidad visual. ¿Puede la tecnología ayudar a disfrutar de una obra de arte sin depender constantemente del teléfono móvil o de la […] La entrada Las Ray-Ban Meta llegan a los museos para acercar el arte a las personas ciegas y con baja visión se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
La Pinacoteca de Brera, en Milán, ha puesto en marcha Sensing Art, un proyecto piloto que combina gafas inteligentes, audiodescripción e inteligencia artificial para facilitar una visita más autónoma a las personas con discapacidad visual.

¿Puede la tecnología ayudar a disfrutar de una obra de arte sin depender constantemente del teléfono móvil o de la ayuda de otra persona? Esta es una de las preguntas a las que busca responder Sensing Art – Capolavori oltre lo sguardo , una iniciativa presentada en octubre de 2026 por Meta, EssilorLuxottica y la Pinacoteca de Brera, en colaboración con organizaciones italianas vinculadas a la discapacidad visual.

El proyecto incorpora gafas inteligentes con inteligencia artificial al recorrido accesible que el museo ya ofrecía a través de su aplicación Grande Brera. El objetivo es facilitar que las personas ciegas y con baja visión descubran algunas de las obras de su colección mediante descripciones sonoras y herramientas de asistencia integradas en las propias gafas.

El recorrido incluye ocho obras de arte seleccionadas de la colección de la Pinacoteca de Brera. Cuando la persona visitante se sitúa ante una de ellas, puede activar desde las gafas el reconocimiento de la obra y escuchar la audiodescripción correspondiente a través de los altavoces integrados en las patillas.

Una de las particularidades de la iniciativa es que no se limita a generar descripciones mediante inteligencia artificial. Las gafas se integran con la aplicación Grande Brera y permiten acceder a los contenidos del método DescriVedendo, desarrollado por la Associazione Nazionale Subvedenti (ANS).

Este método transforma en palabras los elementos visuales de una obra, como sus formas, su composición y sus detalles, para facilitar que las personas con discapacidad visual puedan construir una representación mental de lo que tienen delante.

Para cada una de las ocho obras se ofrecen tres tipos de contenido:

El recorrido también incorpora breves indicaciones sonoras para orientarse entre una obra y otra.

Además de acceder a las audiodescripciones, las personas participantes pueden utilizar otras herramientas integradas en las gafas.

Por un lado, Meta AI permite formular preguntas sobre el contexto y el entorno. Por otro, la integración con Be My Eyes ofrece la posibilidad de contactar con voluntarios videntes y operadores cualificados para recibir asistencia en tiempo real durante la visita y en determinadas tareas prácticas.

Las gafas cuentan con altavoces de oído abierto, que permiten escuchar los contenidos sin aislar completamente a la persona del sonido ambiente. Esto resulta especialmente relevante en un museo, donde mantener la percepción de las conversaciones y de los sonidos del entorno puede contribuir a una experiencia más natural.

La propuesta busca reducir la necesidad de manipular el teléfono móvil durante el recorrido y facilitar que cada visitante gestione los contenidos a su ritmo.

Uno de los aspectos destacados de Sensing Art es la participación de organizaciones y personas con discapacidad visual en el desarrollo y las pruebas de la experiencia.

Junto a Meta, EssilorLuxottica y la Pinacoteca de Brera participan la Associazione Nazionale Subvedenti (ANS), la Unione Italiana dei Ciechi e degli Ipovedenti (UICI) y la Fondazione Istituto dei Ciechi di Milano.

Esta colaboración es importante porque la accesibilidad no depende únicamente de disponer de tecnología avanzada. También requiere comprobar que las herramientas responden a las necesidades reales de quienes van a utilizarlas y que los contenidos son comprensibles, útiles y adecuados para cada situación.

En este caso, las gafas se incorporan a un recorrido accesible que ya existía, en lugar de sustituir el trabajo previo de audiodescripción y adaptación de contenidos.

Sí. El proyecto está abierto al público mediante reserva previa. Según la información publicada por la Pinacoteca de Brera, las gafas se facilitan gratuitamente a las personas ciegas o con baja visión que participan en el recorrido.

El servicio está disponible de martes a viernes, de 10:00 a 16:30 horas, en las condiciones indicadas por el museo.

Para solicitar la reserva, hay que escribir a [email protected] , indicando el día y la hora de la visita, así como las necesidades específicas de apoyo logístico.

La información actualizada puede consultarse en la web oficial de la Pinacoteca de Brera .

La iniciativa abre nuevas posibilidades para acercar el patrimonio cultural a las personas con discapacidad visual. Sin embargo, conviene distinguir entre las prestaciones de un proyecto piloto y una solución que pueda utilizarse de forma generalizada en cualquier museo.

Sensing Art se desarrolla en un museo concreto, con ocho obras seleccionadas y un sistema integrado con sus propios contenidos. Por tanto, no significa que cualquier persona que tenga unas gafas inteligentes de Meta pueda acceder automáticamente a este mismo recorrido en otros espacios culturales.

Tampoco elimina la necesidad de contar con audiodescripciones de calidad, información accesible, orientación adecuada y personal formado.

Su interés reside en explorar cómo la tecnología portátil puede complementar los recursos existentes y ofrecer nuevas formas de interactuar con el arte.

La experiencia de Milán plantea una cuestión importante para el futuro de los museos: cómo aprovechar la inteligencia artificial y las tecnologías portátiles para que las personas ciegas y con baja visión puedan acceder a la cultura con mayor autonomía y construir su propia relación con las obras.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuente: Pinacoteca Di Brera .

es.title: Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.3
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la rc 1 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access. A menos … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la rc 1 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . A menos que se detecten fallos críticos de última hora, esta versión será idéntica a la versión final de NVDA 2026.3. Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta rc te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta rc, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 rc 1 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es f233fe4c2134560c3b945e94ce4c1835a62c511fa22a64bdaa521289bedccc3d. ¡Feliz miércoles!

La entrada Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: What’s New In TalkBack 17.1
en.summary: Google is rolling out version 17.1 of the TalkBack screen reader. Here’s what the new version brings. Selection Mode That Works Only With Chrome It…
en.body:
Published 20 October 2026 by Kareen Kiwan

Google is rolling out version 17.1 of the TalkBack screen reader . Here’s what the new version brings.

Table of Contents

It is now possible to select text outside edit boxes, but the feature is quite limited. Although Google states in the feature overview that it works on webpages, the feature is only supported in the Google Chrome browser. I tested it with Vivaldi, which is a Chromium-based browser like Google Chrome, but text selection didn’t work there.

In Chrome, you should be able to select all the text on a page or start selection mode using the assigned gesture, (by default, double-tapping and holding with two fingers). Once selection mode is active, you can select text using reading controls, as you would in edit boxes. Select all and Start selection mode are available as screen reader actions, so you can also invoke them using actions.

When I tested the feature on a webpage in Chrome, I was far from impressed. The implementation is still unreliable. Moving the focus to the next item while selecting text is not reflected in the text I cycle through using reading controls. Although the focus moves automatically when the end of the current focus is reached while selecting, the movement is not smooth and could result in having to perform the gesture several times without any text being spoken or selected. Additionally, I couldn’t find a way to pause selection without losing what has already been selected. This means you cannot select different parts of a page and append them to a single selection.

Moreover, I noticed that occasionally, I may start selection mode and hear the announcement that I am selecting by character, only to find that after I swipe down to select the next character, a larger portion of the text is selected instead.

One additional thing worth mentioning regarding selection is that it is now possible to assign gestures and keyboard shortcuts to read the selected text or to move the cursor to the start and end of the selection.

TalkBack 17.1 adds a new section to Sound and Feedback settings that allows you to select a different voice from the one you are currently using. You can also assign a gesture to open this section directly.

As is customary with Google , the feature only works with Google’s own TTS engine. When testing it with other engines, numbered voices are shown, but pressing Preview on any of them results in the TTS engine reading the text using the voice you are currently using, as if the text were simply passed to the engine. Voice selection has no effect. With Google TTS, however, voices can be changed without any issues, although I noticed that voice previews did not work during my testing.

The settings section includes an option to install more languages, which allows you to open other engines on your device. However, selecting Acapela, for example, opened the Acapela app without having any practical effect on voice selection.

For people who have been hoping to change TTS engines on the fly when a TTS engine crashes, you will be disappointed.

During the new features tour, TalkBack tells you that you can toggle Guided Vision through a button or later using the Guided Vision shortcut in the TalkBack menu. Using either of these methods does nothing. Trying the Guided Vision shortcut in the TalkBack menu several times returned me to the window I was in without toggling anything.

It is now possible to assign any TalkBack action to a braille display command. The list now extends beyond the actions included in TalkBack 17.0 to include all assignable TalkBack actions. To customize braille commands, go to Braille display settings, then Braille display commands. There, you can find all the actions that can be assigned to braille display commands, including those that are already assigned.

You can change a command if it is already assigned or assign a new command if none is assigned. You can also reset a command to its default setting or remove the assigned command.

In TalkBack 17.1, there are more fields and controls in which browse mode is turned off when using Smart Browse mode. It is also easier to take advantage of a website’s built-in keyboard shortcuts, such as using the arrow keys to expand an item in a tree view. I haven’t tested how Smart Browse mode works in the new version compared to the previous version.

It is now possible to assign a gesture to spell the current focus using Phonetic spelling, so you hear the phonetic example after hearing the letter, such as T, Tango. It is also possible to trigger Phonetic spelling by default through the Action + R + C keyboard shortcut.

More information will now be provided to help distinguish between characters on Chinese, Japanese, and Korean keyboards when using a physical keyboard.

The bug that prevented the Find Voice command from finding matching items has been fixed in the new release.

Published in General

es.title: NaviLens llega al transporte público de Melbourne para mejorar la accesibilidad de las personas ciegas
es.summary: Vision Australia ha destacado el uso de NaviLens en la red de tranvías de Melbourne. Esta tecnología permite localizar señalización mediante el móvil y recibir información del transporte en audio, texto y respuesta háptica. La iniciativa toma como referencia la ruta 96 y abre el debate sobre cómo mejorar la orientación de las personas con […] La entrada NaviLens llega al transporte público de Melbourne para mejorar la accesibilidad de las personas ciegas se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Vision Australia ha destacado el uso de NaviLens en la red de tranvías de Melbourne. Esta tecnología permite localizar señalización mediante el móvil y recibir información del transporte en audio, texto y respuesta háptica.

La iniciativa toma como referencia la ruta 96 y abre el debate sobre cómo mejorar la orientación de las personas con discapacidad visual en el transporte público.

Vision Australia incluyó NaviLens en su boletín de tecnología de septiembre de 2026. La organización explica que el sistema ayuda a las personas ciegas o con baja visión a orientarse en la red de tranvías de Melbourne mediante códigos instalados en las paradas.

Estos códigos tienen un diseño visual distintivo y pueden detectarse con la cámara del teléfono móvil. A través de la aplicación, el usuario recibe información sobre el servicio en formatos adaptados a sus necesidades.

El sistema puede proporcionar información mediante audio, texto y respuesta háptica, como vibraciones del teléfono. De esta manera, la persona puede acceder a información del entorno sin depender exclusivamente de los carteles convencionales.

La tecnología no requiere que el usuario enfoque el código como haría con un código QR tradicional. Está diseñada para detectarlo a distancia y mientras se mueve, lo que puede facilitar la localización de señales en espacios concurridos.

La utilidad de NaviLens va más allá de identificar una parada. En el proyecto de Melbourne, los códigos se integran con los sistemas de información de Yarra Trams para ofrecer datos dinámicos sobre los servicios.

Entre sus aplicaciones se encuentran:

Estas posibilidades pueden contribuir a que las personas con discapacidad visual planifiquen sus desplazamientos con mayor autonomía. Sin embargo, NaviLens es una herramienta de apoyo: no sustituye la necesidad de contar con itinerarios accesibles, información fiable y asistencia cuando sea necesaria.

El despliegue de NaviLens en el transporte público de Victoria comenzó en agosto de 2023. Según la documentación del propio sistema, el primer código se instaló en la parada 9, en el cruce de Bourke Street y Spring Street.

La ruta 96, que conecta Brunswick East con St Kilda Beach, fue la primera línea piloto. NaviLens documenta la instalación de más de 3.000 códigos en sus marquesinas y en la flota de tranvías E-Class.

Posteriormente, Yarra Trams anunció la ampliación de la tecnología a más paradas y vehículos de su red. La compañía explicó que el objetivo era mejorar el acceso a la información para los pasajeros ciegos o con baja visión.

No obstante, existe una diferencia entre las fuentes consultadas: el boletín de Vision Australia de septiembre de 2026 indica que el servicio está disponible actualmente en la ruta 96 y que se espera extenderlo a otras rutas. Por su parte, la documentación de NaviLens y Yarra Trams describe una ampliación de los códigos a más vehículos y servicios.

Por este motivo, no conviene afirmar que toda la red dispone actualmente de la misma cobertura. La información disponible confirma el despliegue inicial en la ruta 96 y la extensión a determinados vehículos, pero el alcance actual completo requiere una confirmación más específica del operador.

La tecnología no es nueva en España. NaviLens ya se utiliza en distintos sistemas de transporte público, con aplicaciones adaptadas a las necesidades de cada red.

En Barcelona, Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) utiliza estos códigos en estaciones de metro y paradas de autobús. La información puede incluir el nombre y el código de la parada, las líneas disponibles, el destino de los autobuses, los tiempos de llegada y las posibles incidencias.

En las estaciones de metro, los códigos también pueden describir distintos espacios y servicios, como accesos, vestíbulos, ascensores, andenes y puntos de embarque. Esta información ayuda a las personas con discapacidad visual a orientarse durante sus desplazamientos.

El caso de Melbourne resulta interesante porque muestra cómo la tecnología puede integrarse en la señalización del transporte y conectarse con información operativa actualizada. No se trata únicamente de identificar un lugar, sino de facilitar información útil para tomar decisiones durante el viaje.

La experiencia de Melbourne permite reflexionar sobre una cuestión importante: para que el transporte público sea accesible, no basta con disponer de vehículos adaptados o recorridos sin barreras físicas. También es necesario que las personas puedan localizar las paradas, identificar los servicios y consultar los cambios que se producen durante el trayecto.

Los códigos NaviLens pueden contribuir a cubrir parte de esa necesidad al añadir información digital accesible a la señalización física existente. Además, su uso mediante teléfonos móviles permite ofrecer diferentes formatos de información desde un mismo punto.

Para valorar su impacto real, también es importante analizar la cobertura de los códigos, la actualización de los datos, la facilidad de uso de la aplicación y la experiencia de las propias personas ciegas o con baja visión.

La accesibilidad del transporte público depende de soluciones que funcionen en situaciones reales. Iniciativas como la de Melbourne y las implantaciones españolas muestran cómo la tecnología puede ayudar a reducir las barreras de información y favorecer desplazamientos más autónomos.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuentes: Vision Australia , Navilens .

es.title: Ya disponible la sexta beta de NVDA 2026.3
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 6 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la sexta beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la sexta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 6 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 6 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 407cd4afb19d72b533c7a88a7eda86fb38d8aa753134b1000a4b6f6275fc172d. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la sexta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: Life In Nature
en.summary: An immersive 3D audio survival game. Craft, hunt, and explore a ruined world. Important: This is an audiogame. The game is played entirely with sound…
en.body:
Published 18 October 2026 by neirin

An immersive 3D audio survival game. Craft, hunt, and explore a ruined world.

Important: This is an audiogame. The game is played entirely with sound and has no visuals. It is designed for the blind and visually impaired community. The screen will be black during gameplay—this is intentional. Headphones are recommended for the best experience.

After a global escalation in science and military technology, the world powers engaged in a catastrophic war. Nuclear explosions altered Earth’s atmosphere, and massive solar storms destroyed all electronic systems. Most of the planet flooded, leaving survivors with only medieval-level resources to endure the harsh new world.

Developed by AudioWander, Life in Nature is a fully 3D spatial-audio multiplayer game specifically designed with accessibility in mind for blind and visually impaired players. In this unforgiving world, survival is your only goal.

Survive the Wild

Every step you take matters. You must carefully manage your Health, Energy, Hunger, and Thirst. Gather wood to build fires, hunt wild animals like bears, boars, and wolves, butcher their meat, and cook it on a skillet or spit. Find fresh water, boil it in a handmade clay pot, and make tea to restore your energy. But beware—falling from heights, animal attacks, or severe hunger will slowly drain your life.

Deep Crafting System

With electronics gone, you must rely on your hands. Gather raw materials from the earth to craft essential tools. Combine items in your hands to weave fishing nets, forge swords and crossbows, or build a sturdy wooden shelter to protect yourself. From a simple stone spear to a complex boat to cross the oceans, everything is built from scratch.

Explore Unique Maps

Navigate entirely by sound and compass directions (North, South, East, West). Explore diverse environments including the Central Valley, dense Bear and Rain forests, scorching deserts, snowy mountain peaks, and deep oceans. Dive underwater to collect oysters or explore hidden caves. Listen closely to your environment—the sound of your footsteps and the ambient noise will guide you.

Challenging Quests & Puzzles

Embark on dangerous quests like “The Lost Miner,” “A Curious Bloom,” or “The Coral Crown.” Jump across perilous chasms, climb steep cliffs, dive into deep underwater tunnels, and search for lost notes and ancient treasures hidden across the world.

Multiplayer & Combat

You are not alone in this ruined world. Meet other survivors, trade resources, and communicate via radio. If you feel brave, activate “PK Mode” (Player Kill) or join or create PK arenas to engage in high-risk, high-reward PvP combat using swords, shotguns, and shields. Team up with trusted friends to hunt dangerous predators or survive the deadly PK map.

Key Features

Put your headphones on, sharpen your senses, and start your new Life in Nature.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

When you launch the game for the first time, it will begin downloading the sounds required to play. Keep your screen reader active during this process so you can hear the download progress. If you leave the game window for any reason, the download will pause until you return.

Once the sounds have finished downloading, the game will launch. At this point, you can disable your screen reader because the game is fully self-voiced.

During account creation, there is a button that sends an account verification code to your email address. After requesting the code, reactivate your screen reader, open your email, copy the verification code, return to the game, paste it into the appropriate field, and then disable your screen reader again.

You can also use a Bluetooth keyboard if the touch gestures are difficult to use. Keyboard shortcuts are available directly from the main menu.

Before playing, make sure you read the rules in their entirety. After finishing the rules, perform a two-finger swipe down with your screen reader to locate the Accept button.

The main menu includes a button for purchasing credits. When you double-tap this button, reactivate your screen reader because the game opens Chrome or your default web browser to complete the transaction through PayPal or another supported payment service.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

2.24. Android 16

Chimege Sonur is a Mongolian text reader for smartphones, developed to make Mongolian text accessible to visually impaired users. It provides Mongolian text-to-speech support so users can read on Android devices using speech output.

The project was developed by Chimege Systems as part of an initiative supporting the participation and access to services of people with disabilities in Mongolia.

en.title: Sortalis
en.summary: Sortalis is a dice-building roguelike inspired by Farkle. Roll, score, and decide how far you’re willing to push your luck—then spend your winnings on Charms and upgrades that transform your dice, strengthen your strategy, and rewrite the rules. en.title: In-Process 16th October 2026
en.summary: We’ve got a bumper edition for you this week, with new content for just about everyone! Accessibility Testing with NVDA NV Access Survey New Help Options for NVDA Users Help for Low Vision Users Free Sample Accessibility Testing with NVDA NVDA 2026.3 Beta 5 Accessibility Testing with NVDA NV Access is very pleased to announce… Read More
en.body:
We’ve got a bumper edition for you this week, with new content for just about everyone!

NV Access is very pleased to announce the release of a new training package. Accessibility Testing with NVDA is designed for people using NVDA to test apps and websites for accessibility.

This Accessibility Testing with NVDA package includes: A training module with over 60 topics in nine sections Getting Started Setting up NVDA Reading information Visual Options Keyboard navigation Navigating content with NVDA Working with elements Testing with a screen reader Reporting Issues A printable NVDA Reference Sheet, with the commands most useful for accessibility testing A printable guide to writing accessible content on a single, printable sheet for easy consultation A list of NV Access and external resources and links to further your knowledge A WCAG 2.2 Reference with tips on testing many of the criteria with NVDA A JPG Badge you can proudly display in your email, or on your website or elsewhere to indicate your support

The purchase price of the module is A$250 (+GST for Australian buyers). Not only do you get a wealth of accessibility testing information, the cost of this package also supports the work of NV Access and helps continue our ability to provide the NVDA screen reading software free of charge.

Please note that this package is useable by both sighted and screen reader users. It is aimed at professionals wanting to test websites, documents and programs for accessibility. If you would like to learn to use NVDA from scratch as a blind or low vision screen reader user, please first consider “ Basic Training for NVDA ” or the “ NVDA Productivity Bundle “.

The Accessibility Testing with NVDA module is designed to teach you to incorporate NVDA into your accessibility testing workflow. It is not intended to replace dedicated accessibility testing tools which can give specific information about testing criteria and compliance etc. If you would like more formal training specifically in web accessibility, we recommend Learn.Intopia.digital . Intopia provided feedback on the web accessibility components of this material.

Please head to Accessibility Testing with NVDA to read more and purchase the new package.

Cover image of “Accessibility Testing with NVDA”

The NVDA Satisfaction Survey 2026 is open, but only until early next week.

We are always interested in understanding the satisfaction of our NVDA users, what is important to you & what we can do more effectively. The survey is anonymous & we encourage you to leave comments in your response.

We’re interested in hearing from as many people as possible, so please feel free to pass this on to others.

The survey is short, only three questions – we deliberately do that in order to make it less onerous to fill out. The rating is a simple, and industry standard metric (a “net promoter score”) we can use to benchmark broadly how well we are doing compared to previous years. We leave room for you to add your own thoughts, so you can give feedback on that one specific point on your mind. If you want a response, please do include your email address as we don’t otherwise collect contact details.

We do sometimes get questions like “It would be great if NVDA had feature X” and it’s frustrating to not be able to reply, especially when NVDA does in fact have feature X, but we have no way to reach the person to share that with them. We have also been asked “Why don’t you ask more questions about X, Y, or Z?” – which is a great question. This survey is designed to collect feedback on everything overall, and we try to keep it fairly consistent from year to year. We do conduct specific surveys from time to time, both more formally, and occasionally just a simple question on Mastodon asking, “What do you think about …”. We like to think we are approachable and easy to get in contact with, so do please always reach out if there is something you’d like to give feedback on or to ask.

Please do head over to https://www.nvaccess.org/survey2026 and fill out the survey if you haven’t already.

We are always looking for ways to help users and make more information available, and easy to find. For many years, the navbar of the NV Access website has had a “Get Help” option. This has linked to a single page of really useful information for NVDA users , including the training material, user groups, how to report an issue or get extra voices, and an FAQ. Now, we have expanded it to a menu. The first item lets you get help for “NVDA Users” and is the original “Get Help” item.

There are also several new options, which are covered below:

With the release of the magnifier in NVDA 2026.2, it seemed a good time to collate some of the features and settings in NVDA which can be useful for low vision users. The way low vision users will have NVDA setup may be different to how a totally blind user who does not use the screen may have it setup. This “ Get Help for Low Vision Users ” page includes information about: The magnifier: including a demo video, list of keystrokes, and link to the comparison with Windows Magnifier we did here in In-Process. Visual Highlighter: How to turn it on and just what the different colours mean. How to reduce speech: Turning on or off individual elements, or adjusting the speech mode overall. Working on the Web: Tips for navigating web pages, and copying information from the web. Other Windows Settings: Suggestions for other Windows settings which can be useful for low vision users.

To go with the brand-new Accessibility Testing with NVDA package , we have made a free sample of the material available. This extensive sample is full of web accessibility tips and tricks with the world’s favourite free screen reader, and is still only a small taste of the full product.

Do check out the Accessibility Testing with NVDA sample page in the new revamped “Get Help” menu. If you find it useful, you will find even more in the full Accessibility Testing with NVDA package , plus you will be supporting us to keep NVDA available for free to everyone who can use it.

Once again, our thanks to Intopia.Digital for their ongoing support of NV Access.

Finally, this week, we’re now up to Beta 5 of NVDA 2026.3 . Last In-Process we were up to Beta 2, so here’s what’s been in the latest three updates:

Changes introduced in Beta 5: Updates to translations Added bug fix for NVDA failing to start on Windows versions older than Windows 10 1903

Changes introduced in Beta 4: Updates to translations Added bug fix for lag in the Add-on Store when searching using Chinese characters Minor documentation changes

Changes introduced in Beta 3: Updates to translations Reverted bug fix to terminals, meaning NVDA may freeze again when substantial amounts of text are dumped to the screen. This is due to the bug fix not working correctly Prevented Magnifier crash recovery from flashing to reduce seizure risk

That’s all for this week. It’s not often the latest beta gets bumped to the SIXTH article in the blog! That by no means reflects on its value though – Please do try NVDA 2026.3 Beta 5 if you haven’t already. If you do any web accessibility work, please do check out the new Accessibility Testing with NVDA Package . It will be around release time for NVDA 2026.3 by next edition, so we’ll have more on the new version. And we’ll also cover a bit more for our low vision users as well.

en.title: From Word to Teams: Using ZoomText and Fusion Across Your Workday
en.summary: ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech. Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful …
en.body:
ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech.

Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful features of ZoomText and Fusion that will help you be more productive in the workplace. This blog series will run throughout October, with a new post every Thursday featuring helpful information and practical tips to make the most of ZoomText and Fusion as you work.

For many professionals, the workday is a journey through Microsoft Office and a variety of collaboration tools. Whether you’re writing, analyzing data, managing emails, or joining virtual meetings, having ZoomText or Fusion set up to support your workflow can make all the difference. This week, we’ll look at how these tools can help you work more efficiently and comfortably, from your first document to your last video call.

Drafting reports or editing proposals is easier when you can see exactly what you need. With ZoomText, you can quickly adjust your magnification level or switch between different zoom window types—like Lens or Line view—to focus on the text that matters most. For longer documents, AppReader is a helpful feature: just press CAPS LOCK+ALT+A to have the text read aloud, letting you follow along visually or simply listen and rest your eyes.

Fusion users can also take advantage of JAWS navigation commands, such as jumping between headings or moving by paragraph, to quickly scan and organize content. To jump by heading, first turn on Quick Navigation keys by pressing CAPS LOCK+Z , then press H to navigate forward through headings or SHIFT+H to navigate backward. Press P to navigate forward by paragraph and SHIFT+P to navigate backward. Press CAPS LOCK+Z to toggle Quick Navigation keys off again so you can continue editing your document.

Keyboard Echo is another useful feature, giving you spoken feedback as you type, so you can be sure your edits are accurate.

To cycle through the different Keyboard Echo settings, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+K . The setting No Echo disables all keyboard echo. Keys will echo your keystrokes as you type. Words will echo individual words as you type them. And Keys and Words will echo both keystrokes and words as you type.

Spreadsheets can be intimidating, but ZoomText’s magnification tools help you zero in on the data you need. Adjust your zoom to see more or less of your sheet and use Reading Zones to mark important areas—like totals or headers—so you can return to them instantly.

A reading zone is a defined area of an application window that ZoomText can display, speak, or both, at the press of a hotkey. To create a reading zone, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+C , then drag a rectangle over the area of the application window you want the zone to cover. To trigger a reading zone, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+ the zone’s number (1 through 9, or 0 for zone 10).

Fusion users can rely on JAWS table navigation to move efficiently through rows and columns, with commands like CAPS LOCK+C to read the current cell, helping you keep your place in complex data.

Staying on top of emails and appointments is simple with the right tools. AppReader lets you listen to long emails, while Focus Enhancements in ZoomText highlight your current selection, making it easier to track where you are.

AppReader reads documents, web pages, and email aloud while you follow along or rest your eyes. It can read from beginning to end, skim forward and backward, or read just the text you select with the mouse. AppReader reads text aloud in three modes: App View reads directly in the source application without changing your view, Text View reformats the text with your choice of fonts, colors, and magnification for easier reading, and the SpeakIt Tool reads any text on the screen that you select by clicking and dragging. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+A to launch App View. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+T to launch Text View. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+S to launch the SpeakIt Tool.

Focus enhancements highlight the item you are on as you navigate using the Tab and arrow keys through menus, dialogs, and toolbars, making it easy to keep your place. Press CAPS LOCK+F to toggle focus enhancements on and off.

Fusion users can use commands like CTRL+N to create a new message, CTRL+R to reply to a message, or CTRL+F to forward a message. You can also switch to different areas in Outlook with quick shortcuts like CTRL+1 to go to your current mail folder, CTRL+2 to navigate to the calendar, and CTRL+3 to go to Contacts.

Whether you’re building slides or presenting to your team, ZoomText’s flexible magnification ensures you can see every detail. AppReader can read slide content aloud, making it easier to review your work or follow along during a presentation. Fusion users can use the arrow keys with JAWS to navigate slides and read speaker notes, so you’re always prepared and in control. Press F6 in PowerPoint to navigate the different areas of your presentation.

Today’s workplace relies on video conferencing apps like Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Google Meet. With ZoomText and Fusion, you can adjust your magnification to follow chat messages, participant panels, and shared screens during meetings. AppReader and JAWS speech help you keep up with notifications and chat without missing a beat.

A standout feature for video calls is Face-in-View . Before joining a meeting, open the Face-in-View tool in Fusion by pressing INSERT+SPACE, F , then O . This feature uses your webcam to show you a live preview and provides feedback to help you center your face and check your lighting—so you can join every call looking your best and feeling confident.

Join us next week as we explore how ZoomText and Fusion can help you access more online, making web browsing and digital resources easier and more accessible. Stay tuned for more tips to help you thrive in your workplace!

Have questions? Email training@vispero.com .

With the right setup and a few helpful features, ZoomText and Fusion can empower you to work smarter and more comfortably, every step of the way.

es.title: Ya disponible la quinta beta de NVDA 2026.3
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 5 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la quinta beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la quinta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 5 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 5 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es c1d2cc7bc21126a224fdc0733fef5f20adf212d6098fd31863c89f7d05195544. ¡Feliz miércoles!

La entrada Ya disponible la quinta beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: Welcome Home: Apple Announces Updated HomePod Mini, Apple TV, All-New HomeView, and New Home Accessories
en.summary: Apple today announced updated models of the HomePod Mini and Apple TV 4K ; as well as an all-new HomeView smart home hub and a collection of smart home accessories . HomePod Mini 2 Powered by the S10 chip and what Apple calls "advanced computational audio," up to four HomePod Mini 2 or HomePod (2nd generation) speakers can be paired to create a surround sound experience with the new Apple TV 4K. Siri AI will be available on HomePod Mini 2 with a future software update. It can recognize up to six people in a household, and can use a user's Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone or iPad to draw on their personal context. With Sound Glow, the top of HomePod Mini 2 can glow and pulse in sync with the currently playing song. Users can additionally customize the displayed animations to promote a relaxing atmosphere. HomePod Mini 2 features 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, and 100 percent recycled copper, gold plating, and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today in pink, green, blue, white and midnight for US $149, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, October 30. HomeView HomeView is a smart home hub with a speaker and 7-inch display, which can either be placed on a table or mounted on a wall. It features a variety of Apple apps and widgets on the Home Screen, and allows users to play music, view photos and videos, make and receive FaceTime calls, monitor and control their home, and more using Siri or the touch interface. HomeView can display a generic screen for everyone in the household, or recognize up to six faces to show personalized content for individual users. Apple Silicon and HomeView's speaker array can optimize audio for loudness and bass response at any volume, with tailored profiles for the table-top and wall-mounted models. Siri AI can be used to play media on HomeView, answer general knowledge questions, discuss recipes, and if a user has an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone or iPad, draw on their personal context for more helpful responses. Like other Apple Intelligence-capable devices, conversations with Siri AI on HomeView are synced via iCloud and viewable in the Siri app on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. Changes made to Siri's pace or expressiveness on compatible devices are synced to HomeView. HomeView features a wide variety of watchOS-style faces that can display snippets of information at a glance, a user's photos, or interactive art. With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView can integrate with compatible cameras to recognize people, pets, packages, and vehicles, and can describe captured video using AI. With Sound Recognition, HomeView can alert users to smoke and carbon monoxide detectors on their iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. Similar to the security and privacy features of other Apple products, data processed by the A18 chip's Secure Exclaves is isolated from the HomeView software and does not leave the device. Users' personal content, like messages and calendar, is only displayed when the user's face is recognized and their iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked. The wall-mounted HomeView model can optionally be professionally installed. HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for US $299, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 13. The table-top model is available in silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray finishes, with the wall-mounted model available in space gray and silver finishes. Apple TV 4K With the A19 chip, Apple claims the new Apple TV 4K delivers up to 50 percent faster CPU performance and up to 2X faster GPU performance when compared to the previous generation. In addition, a new, dedicated AV1 decoder enables more efficient streaming while using less bandwidth. Continuing on the theme of recent Apple product unveilings, the new Apple TV 4K supports Siri AI for smarter voice interactions. Users can find entertainment and control their smart home with more flexible natural language, and Siri AI's awareness of personal context and onscreen content can be used to answer questions about home events or what's currently playing. Users with an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone or iPad will be able to use Siri AI on Apple TV 4K (2nd and 3rd generation). Three far-field microphones on the new Apple TV 4K support Siri hands-free, allowing users to prompt it by saying "Siri" or "Hey Siri," as they do on other Apple devices. The new Siri Remote supports Find My with Precision Finding, which can guide users to the remote's precise location, useful if it, for example, falls between couch cushions. Like other Find My-capable devices, the remote can also play a sound to help users locate it. Similar to other Apple products, data processed by the Secure Exclaves is isolated from tvOS and does not leave the device. The new Apple TV 4K features 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for US $299, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 13. Home Collection In collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric, Apple has launched a collection of smart home accessories, including a lock, doorbell, thermostats, temperature sensors, and indoor and outdoor cameras. These accessories support NFC for one-tap setup on iPhone, and will begin rolling out in December.
en.body: Apple today announced updated models of the HomePod Mini and Apple TV 4K ; as well as an all-new HomeView smart home hub and a collection of smart home accessories .

Reading and listening:

Paperback has two ways to read a document. In text mode, you read the text with your screen reader. In read aloud mode, Paperback reads the text to you with the voice you pick in Settings, and keeps going in the background and from the lock screen. Switch between them from the More Options menu. Audio books, like DAISY, M4B, and MP3 books, play their own recording instead.

The reading bar:

The bar at the bottom of the screen has, from left to right:

You can also swipe up or down on the play button to move by the navigation unit, without reaching for the previous and next buttons. If that is all you use, the Hide previous and next buttons setting takes them out of your screen reader’s way. The Swipe up moves forward setting picks which way a swipe goes.

More options

The More Options menu is where everything else lives.

Keyboards and headsets:

With a keyboard, the desktop shortcuts for opening books, recent documents, Find, Go To, the table of contents, word count, document info, export, and the sleep timer all work. A headset button plays and pauses with one press, moves forward with two, and goes back with three.
